nodes.title: Operations on invertible modules with involution
nodes.statement: Let R be an associative unital ring and M an invertible ℤ-module with involution over R (an R⊗R-module with an involution m ↦ m̄ exchanging the two actions, finitely generated projective for either action, with R → Hom_R(M,M) an isomorphism; GN §6.8a `DerivedCoefficientLine`, Calmès et al. III Definition R.1). (i) For R commutative, every finitely generated projective rank-one R-module L with the identity involution and r⊗s acting by rs is such an M. (ii) For a unit ε ∈ R and an ε-involution on R (a ring isomorphism r ↦ r̄ from R to R^op with r̄̄ = εrε⁻¹ and ε̄ = ε⁻¹), M = R with r⊗s·x = r x s̄ and involution x ↦ ε x̄ is invertible; it is denoted R(ε). (iii) The sign twist −M has the same R⊗R-module and the involution m ↦ −m̄; −R = R(−1) and −(−M) = M. (iv) The dual M^∨ = Hom_R(M,R) is an invertible ℤ-module with involution over R^op.
hypotheses: R associative and unital, not necessarily commutative.
In (ii) the involution is an anti-automorphism up to conjugation by ε, not necessarily involutive.
proofSteps: (i) A rank-one projective L is invertible as an R-module (Mathlib `Module.Invertible`), so R → End_R(L) is bijective; the identity involution exchanges the two equal actions.

(ii) Check the R⊗R-linearity of x ↦ εx̄ against the twisted action r⊗s·x = r x s̄ and that applying it twice is the identity by r̄̄ = εrε⁻¹ and ε̄ = ε⁻¹; R is free of rank one for either action and the unit map is the identity.
(iii) Negating an involution keeps it R⊗R-linear and involutive, and does not change the underlying module, so invertibility is unaffected.
(iv) Hom_R(M,R) is finitely generated projective over R^op because M is finitely generated projective; the involution is transported by precomposition.
acceptance: R(1) for the identity involution on a commutative ring is the symmetric coefficient R with trivial involution, and R(−1) = −R.
M^∨∨ ≅ M canonically, compatibly with the involutions.

nodes.title: Flavoured Grothendieck–Witt and L-spectra of a ring
nodes.statement: For a functor F from Poincaré ∞-categories to spectra (GW, L, or the Tate construction K(−)^{tC₂} on K-theory with the duality action), an invertible ℤ-module with involution M over R and a flavour α ∈ {q, gq, ge, gs, s} ∪ {≥m : m ∈ ℤ}, put F^α(R;M) := F(D^p(R), Q^α_M), where Q^q_M = Q^{≥∞}_M, Q^gq_M = Q^{≥2}_M, Q^ge_M = Q^{≥1}_M, Q^gs_M = Q^{≥0}_M and Q^s_M = Q^{≥−∞}_M (GN §6.8a `genuinePoincareStructure`). For M = R(ε) write F^α(R;ε); for ε = ±1 write F^α(R) := F^α(R;R) and F^{−α}(R) := F^α(R;R(−1)). Homotopy groups are F^α_n(R;M) := π_n F^α(R;M). The connective-cover maps τ_{≥m+1} → τ_{≥m} induce a sequence F^q → ⋯ → F^{≥m+1} → F^{≥m} → ⋯ → F^s, natural in R and M.
hypotheses: F is a functor on Poincaré ∞-categories; the comparison maps exist because Q^{≥m+1}_M → Q^{≥m}_M are Poincaré functors with identity underlying functor.
proofSteps: The structures Q^{≥m}_M and the maps between them are GN §6.8a; applying F to the identity Poincaré functors gives the comparison maps.
The superscript −α refers to the coefficient R(−1), not to a negated degree.
acceptance: L^gs_0(ℤ) → L^s_0(ℤ) is the identity on signature, while L^gq_0(ℤ) → L^gs_0(ℤ) is multiplication by 8 (GN §6.10a).

nodes.title: When consecutive genuine structures agree
nodes.statement: Write Ĥ^k(C₂;M) := π_{−k}(HM^{tC₂}) for the Tate cohomology of the underlying ℤ[C₂]-module of M. If Ĥ^{−m}(C₂;M) = 0 for some m ∈ ℤ, then τ_{≥m+1}HM^{tC₂} → τ_{≥m}HM^{tC₂} is an equivalence, hence so are Q^{≥m+1}_M → Q^{≥m}_M and the induced maps GW(R;Q^{≥m+1}_M) → GW(R;Q^{≥m}_M) and L(R;Q^{≥m+1}_M) → L(R;Q^{≥m}_M). As Ĥ^*(C₂;M) is 2-periodic, the same then holds for every m + 2k. If 2 ∈ R^× all members of the family coincide. If R is commutative and 2-torsion free and M = R with trivial involution, then Ĥ^0(C₂;−R) = 0 and Ĥ^{−1}(C₂;R) = 0, so Q^ge_{−R} = Q^gs_{−R} and Q^gq_R = Q^ge_R.
hypotheses: M invertible ℤ-module with involution over R.
Tate cohomology of the underlying abelian group with C₂-action, π_{−k} convention.
proofSteps: The fibre of τ_{≥m+1}E → τ_{≥m}E is Σ^m Hπ_m E; with E = HM^{tC₂}, π_m E = Ĥ^{−m}(C₂;M) (RefinedTraceMethods RT.2/tate-of-eilenberg-maclane).

Q^{≥m}_M is the pullback of Q^s_M along Map_R(−,τ_{≥m}HM^{tC₂}) → Map_R(−,HM^{tC₂}) (GN §6.8a), so an equivalence of covers gives an equivalence of Poincaré structures with the same duality, hence of GW and L.
Ĥ^*(C₂;−) is 2-periodic (Tau Ceti `Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.tateCohomologyIsoEven`/`IsoOdd`).
If 2 is a unit it acts invertibly and by zero on Tate cohomology, which therefore vanishes.

For an abelian group A with involution σ, Ĥ^0(C₂;A) = ker(1−σ)/im(1+σ) and Ĥ^{−1}(C₂;A) = ker(1+σ)/im(1−σ). For commutative R with trivial involution this gives Ĥ^{−1}(C₂;R) = R[2] (the 2-torsion) and, for −R (σ = −1), Ĥ^0(C₂;−R) = R[2]. Both vanish when R is 2-torsion free, which gives Q^gq_R = Q^ge_R (m = 1) and Q^ge_{−R} = Q^gs_{−R} (m = 0).
acceptance: For R = ℤ: Ĥ^{−1}(C₂;ℤ) = 0, so Q^gq_ℤ = Q^ge_ℤ; Ĥ^1(C₂;ℤ) = 0, so also Q^{≥0}_ℤ = Q^{≥−1}_ℤ; but Ĥ^0(C₂;ℤ) = ℤ/2 ≠ 0, and Q^ge_ℤ → Q^gs_ℤ is not an equivalence (the form ⟨1⟩ is symmetric and not even).
Over ℤ[1/2] all flavours of L coincide.

nodes.title: Shift periodicity of the genuine structures
nodes.statement: For every invertible ℤ-module with involution M over R and every m ∈ ℤ ∪ {±∞}, the loop functor Ω : D^p(R) → D^p(R) refines to an equivalence of Poincaré ∞-categories (D^p(R), (Q^{≥m}_M)[2]) ≃ (D^p(R), Q^{≥m+1}_{−M}), where Q[k] := Σ^k Q. In particular (Q^gs_M)[2] ≃ Q^ge_{−M} and (Q^ge_M)[2] ≃ Q^gq_{−M} after reindexing along Ω, and (Q^s_M)[2] ≃ Q^s_{−M}, (Q^q_M)[2] ≃ Q^q_{−M}.
hypotheses: R discrete (connective suffices); M invertible ℤ-module with involution.
Q[2] is the two-fold suspension of the quadratic functor, not precomposition with a shift.
proofSteps: By Calmès et al. I, Proposition 3.5.3 (with n = 1), Ω refines to an equivalence between (Mod^ω, (Q^α_M)[2]) and the Poincaré structure of the module with genuine involution (𝕊^{1−σ} ⊗ M, Σα): the coefficient is twisted by 𝕊^{1−σ} and the genuine part is suspended once.
Over Hℤ, which is 2σ-oriented, 𝕊^{n−nσ} ⊗ M depends only on the parity of n, and for odd n it is −M (Calmès et al. II, discussion before Corollary 4.3.4); so the coefficient is −M.

Since Tate constructions are invariant under 𝕊^σ ⊗ − (Calmès et al. I, Lemma 3.5.1), (𝕊^{1−σ} ⊗ M)^{tC₂} ≃ Σ M^{tC₂}, and the suspended genuine part Σ(τ_{≥m}M^{tC₂}) = τ_{≥m+1}ΣM^{tC₂} is the genuine part of index m + 1 for R connective; for m = 0, 1 this is Calmès et al. I, Corollary 4.2.24.
For m = ±∞ this is Lurie's observation, recovered at the endpoints.
acceptance: Applied twice: (D^p(R),(Q^{≥m}_M)[4]) ≃ (D^p(R),Q^{≥m+2}_M).
Over an 𝔽₂-algebra −M = M, so the double shift moves m by one without changing M.

nodes.title: Transport of a Poincaré structure to the opposite ring
nodes.statement: The functor X ↦ Hom_R(X,R) is an equivalence of stable ∞-categories D^p(R)^op ≃ D^p(R^op). For a Poincaré structure Q on D^p(R) with duality D, the composite Q^∨ : D^p(R^op)^op ≃ D^p(R) →^D D^p(R)^op →^Q Sp is a Poincaré structure on D^p(R^op), and the underlying functors give an equivalence of Poincaré ∞-categories (D^p(R),Q) ≃ (D^p(R^op),Q^∨). Hence GW(R^op;Q^∨) ≃ GW(R;Q) and L(R^op;Q^∨) ≃ L(R;Q). If Q is compatible with M, Q^∨ is compatible with M^∨.
hypotheses: R any ring; Q any Poincaré structure on D^p(R).
proofSteps: Hom_R(−,R) exchanges finitely generated projective left and right modules and preserves finite complexes, hence perfect objects; its double application is the identity up to the evaluation equivalence.
Pulling Q back along the duality and then along this equivalence gives a quadratic functor whose cross-effect is represented by the transported duality, so it is Poincaré.
By construction the composite functor carries Q^∨ to Q, which is an equivalence of Poincaré ∞-categories; apply GW and L.
acceptance: For a ring with involution and M = R, Q^∨ is again the corresponding structure for R ≅ R^op, so GW(R) ≃ GW(R^op).

nodes.title: Shifted genuine Grothendieck–Witt spectra and symplectic forms
nodes.statement: Let R be commutative and GW^{[n]}(R) := τ_{≥0}GW(D^p(R),(Q^{≥0}_R)[n]). Then GW^{[0]}(R) ≃ GW^s_cl(R), GW^{[2]}(R) ≃ GW^{−ev}_cl(R) and GW^{[4]}(R) ≃ GW^q_cl(R), the classical group completions of symmetric, (−1)-even and quadratic forms. Moreover the (−1)-even forms on a finitely generated projective P are exactly the symplectic forms, the skew-symmetric b with b(x,x) = 0 for all x: Ĥ^0(C₂;Hom_{R⊗R}(P⊗P,R(−1))) ≅ Hom_R(P, φ_*R[2]) where R[2] is the 2-torsion of R with the Frobenius-twisted action r·a = r²a, and a skew-symmetric b maps to x ↦ b(x,x); the norm-lifting obstruction of b is this function, so b lifts exactly when it vanishes on the diagonal.
hypotheses: R commutative.
The twisted module structure on R[2] is the one from the Tate diagonal (correction of Remark R.7, sourceIssues E6).
proofSteps: Apply the shift periodicity HK.0/shift-periodicity once and twice: (Q^gs_R)[2] ≃ Q^ge_{−R} and (Q^gs_R)[4] ≃ Q^gq_R.
Take connective covers and apply the Hebestreit–Steimle comparison of connective genuine GW with classical GW (GN §6.8a `weightHeartGWComparison`).

Compute Ĥ^0 = (invariants)/(norms) for C₂ acting on Hom_{R⊗R}(P⊗P,R(−1)) by b ↦ (x,y ↦ −b(y,x)): the invariants are the skew-symmetric forms and the norms are the forms c(x,y) − c(y,x). The map b ↦ (x ↦ b(x,x)) kills norms, is additive, takes values in R[2] because 2b(x,x) = 0 for skew b, and is linear for r·a = r²a. For P = R it is the identity of R[2] (the invariants are a·xy with 2a = 0 and there are no nonzero norms); additivity in P and passage to retracts give the general case.
Hence a skew-symmetric form lifts along the norm exactly when it vanishes on the diagonal, which is the definition of symplectic.
acceptance: For R = ℤ, symplectic GW₀ is ℤ generated by the hyperbolic alternating plane (GN §6.11.1).
Over 𝔽₂[t] with P = R and b(x,y) = xy, x ↦ b(x,x) = x² is additive and r²-linear, not R-linear.

sources.match: Defines GW^{[n]} as connective covers of the shifted genuine symmetric GW, identifies GW^{[0]}, GW^{[2]}, GW^{[4]} with classical symmetric, (−1)-even and quadratic GW via Hebestreit–Steimle, and shows symplectic forms are the (−1)-even ones through a Tate cohomology computation.

nodes.title: The metabolic Poincaré ∞-category
nodes.statement: For a Poincaré ∞-category (C,Q) with duality D, Met(C,Q) is the arrow category Ar(C) = Fun(Δ¹,C) with the quadratic functor Q^met(w → x) = fib(Q(x) → Q(w)). Its bilinear part is fib(B(x,x′) → B(w,w′)), represented by the duality D^met(w → x) = (fib(Dx → Dw) → Dx), so Met(C,Q) is Poincaré. A hermitian form on f : w → x is a pair (q,η) of a form q ∈ Ω^∞Q(x) and a null-homotopy η of f^*q; it is Poincaré exactly when q^♯ : x → Dx is an equivalence and the induced map x/w → Dw is an equivalence, i.e. when f is a Lagrangian of the Poincaré object (x,q). Thus Pn(Met(C,Q)) is the space Pn^∂(C,Q) of Poincaré objects with a Lagrangian, and forgetting the Lagrangian is induced by the Poincaré functor met : Met(C,Q) → (C,Q), (w → x) ↦ x.
hypotheses: (C,Q) a Poincaré ∞-category in the sense of GN §6.8a (small stable C, Q reduced 2-excisive with represented cross-effect).
proofSteps: Q^met is reduced and 2-excisive as a fibre of two such functors composed with exact functors.
Compute the cross-effect as the fibre of cross-effects and represent it using the duality of C; this exhibits D^met.
Unwind a Poincaré Q^met-form into the square with corners w, fib(Dx → Dw), x, Dx; being an equivalence of arrows is the two conditions stated.
acceptance: On the hyperbolic object hyp(x) the summand inclusion x → x ⊕ Dx is a Lagrangian, so hyp(x) is in the image of Pn(Met).

sources.match: Defines the metabolic category on the arrow category with the fibre quadratic functor, computes its duality, characterises its Poincaré objects as Poincaré objects with a Lagrangian, and constructs the Poincaré functors (C,Q[−1]) → Met(C,Q) → (C,Q).

nodes.title: The Bott–Genauer sequence
nodes.statement: For every Poincaré ∞-category (C,Q) the sequence (C,Q[−1]) → Met(C,Q) → (C,Q), x ↦ (x → 0) and (w → x) ↦ x, is a Poincaré–Verdier sequence (both a fibre and a cofibre sequence of Poincaré ∞-categories). Consequently every Verdier-localising invariant F gives a fibre sequence F(C,Q[−1]) → F(Met(C,Q)) → F(C,Q).
hypotheses: Poincaré–Verdier sequences and Verdier-localising invariants as in GN §6.8a (`PoincareVerdierSequence`, `stableGWVerdierLocalization`).
proofSteps: The functor x ↦ (x → 0) is fully faithful with image the arrows with zero target; this image is closed under the metabolic duality and Q^met restricts to ΩQ (Calmès et al. I, Lemma 2.3.7).

The target functor Ar(C) → C is a Verdier projection with kernel exactly that image (an arrow with zero target is killed), and the Poincaré structure on C is the one induced by left Kan extension along the projection.
Hence the sequence is a Poincaré–Verdier sequence (Calmès et al. II, Example 1.2.5); apply F.
acceptance: For F = GW and C = 0 the sequence is trivially exact.
For F = L, L(Met(C,Q)) = 0 and the sequence gives L(C,Q[−1]) ≃ ΩL(C,Q).

sources.match: Shows that the metabolic sequence (C,Q[−1]) → Met(C,Q) → (C,Q) is a Poincaré–Verdier sequence.
Constructs the two Poincaré functors of the metabolic sequence.
Recalls the Bott–Genauer sequence and that it is a Poincaré–Verdier sequence.

nodes.title: GW of the metabolic category and the forgetful–hyperbolic sequence
nodes.statement: For a Poincaré ∞-category (C,Q), GW(Met(C,Q)) ≃ K(C) naturally, via the Poincaré functors lag : Met(C,Q) ⇄ Hyp(C) : can and the equivalence GW(Hyp(C)) ≃ K(C). Under this identification the Bott–Genauer sequence becomes a fibre sequence of spectra GW(C,Q[−1]) →^{fgt} K(C) →^{hyp} GW(C,Q), where fgt is induced by forgetting the form, Pn(C,Q[−1]) → C^≃, and hyp by the hyperbolic form, C^≃ → Pn(C,Q). Writing U(C,Q) := fib(hyp) and V(C,Q) := fib(fgt), one has U(C,Q) ≃ GW(C,Q[−1]) and V(C,Q) ≃ ΩGW(C,Q[1]), hence V(C,Q) ≃ ΩU(C,Q[2]).
hypotheses: K is the (connective) K-theory of the stable ∞-category C (GeneralAlgebraicKTheoryPartII KII.0); GW the stable GW spectrum of GN §6.8a.
proofSteps: lag and can (the Poincaré functors of Calmès et al. I, Construction 2.3.8) induce inverse equivalences on GW (Calmès et al. II, Corollary 4.3.1, deduced there from its Example 2.3.3 and Corollary 3.1.5).
GW(Hyp(C)) ≃ K(C) by hermitian additivity (GN §6.8a, the check that GW of the hyperbolic category is K).
Apply GW to the Bott–Genauer sequence, which is a Poincaré–Verdier sequence, using that GW is Verdier localising (GN §6.8a `stableGWVerdierLocalization`).
Read off U and V: the fibre of hyp is the first term; the sequence for Q[1] shows that the fibre of fgt : GW(C,Q) → K(C) is ΩGW(C,Q[1]); compare with U(C,Q[2]) ≃ GW(C,Q[1]).
acceptance: For C = D^p(R) and Q = Q^s_M, the composite fgt∘hyp on K₀ is P ↦ [P] + [DP].
For a field F of characteristic ≠ 2 with Q = Q^s_F, on π₀ the map hyp : K₀(F) = ℤ → GW₀(F) sends 1 to the hyperbolic plane and fgt : GW₀(F) → ℤ is the rank, so fgt∘hyp is multiplication by 2.

sources.match: Identifies GW of the metabolic category with K-theory through the hyperbolic category, derives the Bott–Genauer fibre sequence GW(C,Q[−1]) → K(C) → GW(C,Q) and Karoubi's fundamental theorem U(C,Q[2]) ≃ ΣV(C,Q).
States GW(Met(C,Q)) ≃ K(C), the induced fibre sequence with fgt and hyp, and the equivalence V(R;Q) ≃ ΩU(R;Q[2]).

nodes.title: Karoubi periodicity without inverting 2
nodes.statement: Let R be a ring and M an invertible ℤ-module with involution over R. For every m ∈ ℤ there is a natural equivalence V(R;Q^{≥m}_M) ≃ ΩU(R;Q^{≥m+1}_{−M}), where U(R;Q) = fib(K(R) → GW(R;Q)) and V(R;Q) = fib(GW(R;Q) → K(R)) are the fibres of hyp and fgt on D^p(R).
hypotheses: R discrete associative ring; M invertible; m finite (the endpoints are covered by the same argument with m = ±∞).
No assumption on 2.
proofSteps: By HK.1/forgetful-hyperbolic-sequence, V(R;Q^{≥m}_M) ≃ ΩU(R;(Q^{≥m}_M)[2]).

By HK.0/shift-periodicity, Ω : D^p(R) → D^p(R) is an equivalence of Poincaré ∞-categories (D^p(R),(Q^{≥m}_M)[2]) ≃ (D^p(R),Q^{≥m+1}_{−M}); it induces equivalences on K and GW compatible with hyp, hence on U.
Combine (Calmès et al. II, Corollary 4.3.4, specialised to discrete R over Hℤ, which is 2σ-oriented).
acceptance: If 2 ∈ R^×, all Q^{≥m}_M agree and this is Karoubi's theorem V(R;Q^s_M) ≃ ΩU(R;Q^s_{−M}).
The equivalence is natural for maps of rings with compatible modules with involution.

sources.match: States V(R;Q^{≥m}_M) ≃ ΩU(R;Q^{≥m+1}_{−M}) for every ring, invertible M and m, quoting Paper II.
Proves U(Mod^c(R),Q^{≥m+1}_{−M}) ≃ ΣV(Mod^c(R),Q^{≥m}_M) for connective E₁-algebras over a 2σ-oriented base, and the quadratic and symmetric endpoint versions.

nodes.title: Classical special cases of Karoubi periodicity
nodes.statement: (i) If 2 ∈ R^×, V(R;Q^s_M) ≃ ΩU(R;Q^s_{−M}). (ii) If R is commutative and 2-torsion free (for instance a ring of integers of a number field) and M = R with trivial involution, then V(R;Q^gs_R) ≃ ΩU(R;Q^gs_{−R}), V(R;Q^gs_{−R}) ≃ ΩU(R;Q^gq_R) and V(R;Q^gq_R) ≃ ΩU(R;Q^gq_{−R}); moreover V(R;Q^gq_{−R}) ≃ ΩU(R;Q^{≥3}_R).
hypotheses: (ii): R commutative, 2-torsion free; trivial involution on M = R.
proofSteps: (i) HK.1/karoubi-periodicity with all Q^{≥m}_M equal by HK.0/tate-collapse-criterion.

(ii) Apply HK.1/karoubi-periodicity with (M,m) = (R,0), (−R,0), (R,2), (−R,2) and simplify with Q^ge_{−R} = Q^gs_{−R} (Ĥ^0(C₂;−R) = 0), Q^gq_R = Q^ge_R (Ĥ^{−1}(C₂;R) = 0) and Q^{≥3}_{−R} = Q^{≥2}_{−R} = Q^gq_{−R} (Ĥ^{−2}(C₂;−R) = Ĥ^0(C₂;−R) = 0 by 2-periodicity), all from HK.0/tate-collapse-criterion.
acceptance: The last equivalence has Q^{≥3}_R on the right, which is not known to be described by classical forms; it is not identified with Q^gq_R here.

sources.match: Specialises Theorem R.8 when 2 is a unit and for 2-torsion-free commutative rings with M = R, giving three equivalences among the genuine structures and noting that the next one involves Q^{≥3}_R.

nodes.title: Periodicity of bordism-invariant functors on the genuine family
nodes.statement: Let F be a Verdier-localising invariant of Poincaré ∞-categories with F(Met(C,Q)) = 0 for all (C,Q) (bordism invariant). Then F(C,Q[n]) ≃ Σ^n F(C,Q) for all n ∈ ℤ. L-theory and the Tate construction K(C,Q)^{tC₂} are bordism invariant. Consequently, for every ring R, invertible M and m ∈ ℤ ∪ {±∞}, L(R;Q^{≥m}_M) ≃ Ω²L(R;Q^{≥m+1}_{−M}) and K(R;Q^{≥m}_M)^{tC₂} ≃ Ω²K(R;Q^{≥m+1}_{−M})^{tC₂}. In particular L(R;Q^s_M), L(R;Q^q_M) and K(R;M)^{tC₂} are 4-periodic, and 2-periodic when R is an 𝔽₂-algebra; and Σ⁴L^gs(R;M) ≃ L^gq(R;M), Σ²L^gs(R;M) ≃ L^ge(R;−M).
hypotheses: F spectrum-valued, Verdier localising; K(C,Q) the K-theory spectrum of C with the C₂-action induced by the duality.
proofSteps: Bordism invariance and the Bott–Genauer sequence give F(C,Q[−1]) ≃ ΩF(C,Q) (Calmès et al. II, Proposition 3.5.8); iterate. For L this is the integer-shift delooping of GN §6.8a.
L vanishes on metabolic categories by construction of the bordification (GN §6.8a).
K(Met(C,Q)) is the induced C₂-object of K(C) by additivity, so its Tate construction vanishes (RefinedTraceMethods RT.2/tate-vanishing-induced; Calmès et al. II, Example 3.5.7).
Combine with HK.0/shift-periodicity: F(R;Q^{≥m}_M) ≃ Ω²F(R;(Q^{≥m}_M)[2]) ≃ Ω²F(R;Q^{≥m+1}_{−M}).
At m = ±∞ apply twice and use −(−M) = M; over an 𝔽₂-algebra −M = M already.
acceptance: L^s_n(ℤ) is ℤ, ℤ/2, 0, 0 for n ≡ 0,1,2,3 mod 4 and 4-periodic in n (GN §6.10a).
L^gs_{−2}(ℤ) ≅ L^ge_0(ℤ;−1), so Theorem 5's negative range is reached from even forms.

sources.locator: Recollection pp. 10–11 and Corollary R.10, p. 10
sources.match: Explains that bordism-invariant Verdier-localising functors satisfy F(C,Q[n]) ≃ Σ^nF(C,Q), that L and the Tate construction on K are examples, and derives the double-shift periodicity of L and K^{tC₂} on the family Q^{≥m}_M with the 4- and 2-periodicity statements.

nodes.title: r-symmetric and m-quadratic Poincaré structures
nodes.statement: Let Q be a Poincaré structure on D^p(R) compatible with M, i.e. with underlying duality D = Hom_R(−,M). Then the canonical map Q^q_M → Q^s_M factors as Q^q_M → Q → Q^s_M, and Q^q_M, Q^s_M are the initial and the final M-compatible Poincaré structures. For r ∈ ℤ, Q is r-symmetric if for every P ∈ Proj(R) the fibre of Q(P[0]) → Q^s_M(P[0]) is (−r)-truncated; for m ∈ ℤ, Q is m-quadratic if the cofibre of Q^q_M(P[0]) → Q(P[0]) is m-connective. Here a spectrum E is m-connective if π_kE = 0 for k < m and m-truncated if π_kE = 0 for k > m. The fibre and the cofibre are exact functors, so it suffices to test P = R; if Q is r-symmetric the fibre at X is (−r−k)-truncated for every k-connective X, and if Q is m-quadratic the cofibre at X is (m+k)-connective whenever DX is k-connective.
hypotheses: Q M-compatible; M invertible ℤ-module with involution over R.
proofSteps: The factorisation and extremality come from the linear-part description of quadratic functors with fixed bilinear part (Calmès et al. I, Construction 3.2.6 and Corollary 1.3.6; GN §6.8a `poincareLinearPart`).

Fibre and cofibre of maps of reduced quadratic functors with the same bilinear part are linear (exact) functors, so their values are determined on the generator R by finite sums, retracts, shifts and extensions.

Truncatedness is closed under extensions and under Σ^{−1}; connectivity is closed under extensions and Σ; apply this to cell decompositions of k-connective objects (for the symmetric case) and of objects with k-connective dual (for the quadratic case).
acceptance: Q^s_M is r-symmetric for all r; Q^q_M is m-quadratic for all m.

sources.match: Records that M-compatible structures sit between Q^q_M and Q^s_M, defines r-symmetric and m-quadratic structures through truncatedness of the fibre and connectivity of the cofibre on projectives, and reduces to P = R with the propagation to connective objects.
Shows the bilinear-part functor on quadratic functors has fully faithful adjoints, giving the initial and final quadratic functors with given bilinear part.

nodes.title: Bounds for the genuine family
nodes.statement: For every m ∈ ℤ the Poincaré structure Q^{≥m}_M is m-quadratic and (2−m)-symmetric. In particular Q^gs_M is 2-symmetric and 0-quadratic, Q^ge_M is 1-symmetric and 1-quadratic, and Q^gq_M is 0-symmetric and 2-quadratic.
hypotheses: M invertible ℤ-module with involution; m finite.
proofSteps: From the defining pullback (GN §6.8a) there are fibre sequences τ_{≤m−2}ΩHM^{tC₂} → Q^{≥m}_M(R) → Q^s_M(R) and Q^q_M(R) → Q^{≥m}_M(R) → τ_{≥m}HM^{tC₂}.
The first fibre is (m−2)-truncated, i.e. (−(2−m))-truncated; the second cofibre is m-connective.
Apply HK.2/r-symmetric-m-quadratic with P = R.
acceptance: Q^gs_ℤ is in fact 3-symmetric and Q^gq_ℤ = Q^ge_ℤ (HK.0/tate-collapse-criterion), so the bounds are not optimal for every M.

sources.match: Derives from two fibre sequences on R that Q^{≥m}_M is m-quadratic and (2−m)-symmetric, and lists the three genuine cases.

nodes.title: The opposite structure keeps both bounds
nodes.statement: If Q is an M-compatible r-symmetric and m-quadratic Poincaré structure on D^p(R), then Q^∨ (HK.0/opposite-ring-transport) is an M^∨-compatible r-symmetric and m-quadratic Poincaré structure on D^p(R^op).
hypotheses: Q M-compatible on D^p(R).
proofSteps: Under the equivalence of Remark R.11 the map Q^q_{M^∨}(R^op) → Q^∨(R^op) is Q^q_M(M[0]) → Q(M[0]).
M is finitely generated projective, so by HK.2/r-symmetric-m-quadratic the cofibre is m-connective; the symmetric bound is checked the same way on the fibre.
acceptance: For commutative R and M = R with trivial involution, R^op = R, M^∨ = R and the genuine structures satisfy (Q^{≥m}_R)^∨ = Q^{≥m}_R; for a nontrivial line bundle L, L^∨ = L^{−1} ≠ L, so the statement transports bounds between different coefficients.

sources.match: Shows Q^∨ is r-symmetric and m-quadratic when Q is, by evaluating on M[0] and using that M is finitely generated projective.

nodes.title: Connectivity criterion for complexes of bounded width
nodes.statement: For X ∈ D^p(R) and integers k ≤ l the following are equivalent: (i) X is represented by a complex 0 → P_l → ⋯ → P_k → 0 of finitely generated projective R-modules with P_i in homological degree i; (ii) X is k-connective and DX = Hom_R(X,M) is (−l)-connective. The duality is not needed: (ii) may be read with Hom_R(X,R) ∈ D^p(R^op). One-sidedly, X is k-connective exactly when it is represented by a complex of finitely generated projectives vanishing below degree k. If M is free and X ∈ D^f(R), (ii) is equivalent to (i) with stably free P_i; more generally, for Free(R) ⊆ 𝒞 ⊆ Proj(R) closed under duality and sums and X represented by a bounded 𝒞-valued complex, (ii) is equivalent to (i) with each P_i stably in 𝒞.
hypotheses: R any ring; X perfect; M invertible (finitely generated projective in either structure).
proofSteps: (i) ⇒ (ii) is immediate.

For (ii) ⇒ (i) take a representing complex C of minimal length. If C_i ≠ 0 with i < k minimal then H_i(C) = 0, so C_{i+1} → C_i is a surjection of projectives, hence split with projective kernel; replacing C_{i+1} by the kernel and deleting C_i shortens C, a contradiction.

The termwise dual complex (DC)_i = D(C_{−i}) represents DX and is again of minimal length since M is finitely generated projective; the same argument places it in degrees ≥ −l, so C is in degrees ≤ l.
The free and 𝒞-valued refinements run the same argument, where the kernel of a split surjection between stably-𝒞 modules is stably in 𝒞.
acceptance: X = ℤ/2[0] ∈ D^p(ℤ) (resolved by ℤ →² ℤ in degrees [0,1]) is 0-connective and Dℤ/2 ≃ ℤ/2[−1] is (−1)-connective, so it is represented in [0,1] and not in [0,0].
P[0] for P projective is 0-connective with 0-connective dual, so it is represented in [0,0].

sources.match: Proves the equivalence of representability in degrees [k,l] with the connectivity bounds on X and DX by a minimal-length argument, notes that no duality is needed and that connectivity alone gives one-sided representability, and states the stably free and intermediate-subcategory refinements.

nodes.title: Connectivity of an m-quadratic structure on a shifted projective
nodes.statement: If Q is an m-quadratic Poincaré structure on D^p(R), then for every P ∈ Proj(R) and k ∈ ℤ the spectrum Q(P[k]) is min(−2k, m−k)-connective.
hypotheses: Q M-compatible and m-quadratic.
proofSteps: The cofibre of Q^q_M(P[k]) → Q(P[k]) is (m−k)-connective by HK.2/r-symmetric-m-quadratic, since D(P[k]) = (DP)[−k] is (−k)-connective.
Q^q_M(P[k]) = (Hom_{R⊗R}(P⊗P,M)[−2k])_{hC₂} is (−2k)-connective because P is projective and homotopy orbits preserve connectivity (RefinedTraceMethods RT.2/homotopy-orbits-fixed-points).
acceptance: For Q = Q^gs_M (m = 0) and k = −1, Q(P[−1]) is 1-connective since min(2, 1) = 1; for k = 1 the bound is min(−2, −1) = −2.

sources.match: Proves that Q(P[k]) is min(−2k, m−k)-connective for an m-quadratic Q and projective P, from the cofibre bound and connectivity of homotopy orbits.

nodes.title: L-groups as cobordism groups
nodes.statement: Let (C,Q) be a Poincaré ∞-category and n ∈ ℤ. Call Poincaré objects (X,q), (X′,q′) cobordant if (X ⊕ X′, q ⊕ (−q′)) admits a Lagrangian. Cobordism is a congruence for ⊕, the diagonal X → X ⊕ X is a Lagrangian of (X ⊕ X, q ⊕ (−q)), and the set L_n(C,Q) of cobordism classes of Poincaré objects for Q[−n] = Ω^nQ is an abelian group. There is an exact sequence of commutative monoids π₀Pn^∂(C,Q[−n]) → π₀Pn(C,Q[−n]) → L_n(C,Q) → 0, L_n(C,Q) is the cokernel of the boundary map in commutative monoids, and L_n(C,Q) ≅ π_n L(C,Q) for the L-spectrum of GN §6.8a.
hypotheses: (C,Q) Poincaré; Pn^∂ = Pn(Met(C,Q)) is the space of Poincaré objects with a Lagrangian (HK.1/metabolic-category).
proofSteps: Congruence: a sum of Lagrangians is a Lagrangian of the sum.
Diagonal: the diagonal of X → X ⊕ X with the evident null-homotopy of q − q is a Lagrangian (GN 6.2 `symmetric-diagonal-lagrangian` in the exact setting; the same check in the stable setting).

The cokernel in commutative monoids surjects onto the cobordism group with trivial kernel by exactness, and it is a group (Calmès et al. I, Lemma 2.3.10), hence they agree (Calmès et al. I, Definition 2.3.11).
π₀ of the L-spectrum is L₀ (Calmès et al. II, Definition 4.2.6 and its realisation of cobordisms), and π_nL(C,Q) = L₀(C,Q[−n]) by the shift delooping of GN §6.8a.
acceptance: Over a field F of characteristic ≠ 2 with Q = Q^s_F, L₀ is the Witt group of F (HK.4/witt-group-computes-L0 and QuadraticFormInvariants Layer 4).
The hyperbolic object hyp(X) is zero in L₀.

sources.match: Defines cobordism of Poincaré objects and the L-groups of the shifted structures, shows they are abelian groups via the diagonal Lagrangian, records the exact sequence of monoids and compares with the cokernel definition of Paper I.
Proves that the cokernel of π₀Pn^∂ → π₀Pn in commutative monoids is a group and defines the L-groups as these cokernels.
Identifies L₀ with π₀ of the cobordism category and the negative homotopy of GW with L₀ of the shifted structures.

nodes.title: Lagrangian surgery
nodes.statement: Let (L → X, q, η) be a Lagrangian of a Poincaré object (X,q), viewed as a Poincaré object of Met(C,Q). A surgery datum on it is a morphism (Z → W) → (L → X) in Met(C,Q) with a null-homotopy of the pulled-back Q^met-form; algebraic surgery (GN §6.8a) produces a new Poincaré object (L′ → X′, q′, η′) of Met(C,Q), where X′ is the surgery of X along W → X and L′ = fib(L/Z → D(W/Z)) for the metabolic duality. A Lagrangian surgery datum is the case W = 0: a map Z → N := fib(L → X) together with a null-homotopy in ΩQ(Z). Then X′ ≃ X canonically, and there are fibre sequences L′ → L/Z → ΩDZ and N′ → N/Z → ΩDZ with N′ = fib(L′ → X). One then says that L is cobordant to L′ relative to X.
hypotheses: (C,Q) Poincaré; the shift conventions are those of HK.1/metabolic-category.
proofSteps: A morphism (Z → W) → (L → X) in the arrow category with a null-homotopy of the Q^met-form is a surgery datum in Met(C,Q); apply algebraic surgery there (GN §6.8a) and read off the underlying arrow using D^met.

If W = 0 the morphism is the same as a map Z → N, the form condition becomes a null-homotopy in Q^met(Z → 0) = ΩQ(Z), the surgery on the target X is along 0 → X and changes nothing, and the surgery diagram (Calmès et al. III, Remark 1.1.14) gives the two fibre sequences.
acceptance: Surgery along the zero datum returns (L → X).
If Z → N is an equivalence the new Lagrangian L′ is computed from L/N ≃ X.

sources.match: Displays the surgery diagram and constructs Lagrangian surgery as surgery in the metabolic category, with the case of a datum with zero target, the fibre sequences for the new Lagrangian and its fibre, and the notion of Lagrangians cobordant relative to X.

nodes.title: Bounded-width L-monoids
nodes.statement: Let Q be an M-compatible Poincaré structure on D^p(R) and n, a, b ∈ ℤ with a, b ≥ −1, b ≥ a − 1 and n + a even. Pn^a_n(R,Q) ⊆ Pn(D^p(R),Q[−n]) is spanned by the Poincaré objects (X,q) with X ((−n−a)/2)-connective, and M^{a,b}_n(R,Q) ⊆ Pn^∂(D^p(R),Q[−n]) by the Poincaré pairs (L → X, q, η) with X ((−n−a)/2)-connective, L ⌈(−n−1−b)/2⌉-connective and N := fib(L → X) ≃ Ω^{n+1}DL ⌊(−n−1−b)/2⌋-connective (allowed Lagrangians). Define L^{a,b}_n(R;Q) := coker(π₀M^{a,b}_n(R,Q) → π₀Pn^a_n(R,Q)) in commutative monoids. By the width criterion, X is then represented by a complex of projectives in degrees [(−n−a)/2, (−n+a)/2] (width a); for b + n odd both L and N are represented in [(−n−1−b)/2, (−n−1+b)/2]; for b + n even (then b ≥ a) L is represented in [(−n−b)/2, (−n+b)/2] and N in [(−n−b)/2 − 1, (−n+b)/2 − 1]. If b ≥ a the diagonal of (X,q) ⊕ (X,−q) is allowed and L^{a,b}_n(R;Q) is a group; Pn^{−1}_n is contractible. The same definitions make sense for a stable ∞-category with a t-structure (HK.6/t-structure-bounded-l) and for compact modules over a connective ring spectrum (HK.5/ring-spectrum-setting).
hypotheses: Parity: n + a even, so (−n−a)/2 ∈ ℤ.
Connectivity is that of the underlying complex (Postnikov t-structure on D(R)).
proofSteps: Membership is a condition on components, so the subspaces and the monoid map are well defined; direct sums preserve all bounds.
DX ≃ X[n] for a Poincaré object of Q[−n], so the connectivity of X gives that of DX and HK.2/width-criterion gives the representing interval.
For b + n odd the bounds on X and N imply the one on L; for b + n even the bounds on X and L imply the one on N, using DL ≃ N[n+1].
If b ≥ a the diagonal Lagrangian of (X ⊕ X, q ⊕ −q) has L = X, which satisfies the bounds.
acceptance: (n,a,b) = (0,0,1): objects are projective modules in degree 0 and allowed Lagrangians are represented in degrees [−1,0].
(n,a,b) = (n,n,n+1), n ≥ 0: objects in degrees [−n,0] and Lagrangians in [−n−1,0], Ranicki's lengths.

nodes.title: The Witt group of projectives as a bounded L-group
nodes.statement: Let Q be a Poincaré structure on D^p(R) whose duality preserves Proj(R). A Poincaré object (P,q) with P ∈ Proj(R) is strictly metabolic if it has a projective submodule L with q|_L = 0 in π₀Q(L) and 0 → L → P → DL → 0 exact. The Witt group W(Proj(R);Q) is the quotient of π₀Pn^0_0(R,Q) by the submonoid generated by strictly metabolic objects; when Q restricts to an abelian-group-valued functor on Proj(R) it is the classical Witt group of the exact category with duality (GN 6.4 `exact-witt-group`). There is a canonical isomorphism W(Proj(R);Q) ≅ L^{0,0}_0(R;Q).
hypotheses: Duality preserves Proj(R) (true for Q compatible with an invertible M).
proofSteps: It suffices that (P,q) is strictly metabolic iff it admits an allowed Lagrangian of width 0.
An allowed Lagrangian of width 0 is a projective L with fibre DL[−1], i.e. a short exact sequence 0 → L → P → DL → 0 with q|_L null.
Conversely any null-homotopy η of q|_L makes (L → P, η) allowed, because whether the square with corners L, P, 0, DL is cartesian is exactly exactness of the sequence and does not depend on η.
acceptance: For a field F of characteristic ≠ 2 with Q^gs_F this is the usual Witt group W(F) of QuadraticFormInvariants Layer 4.
For ℤ with Q^gs_ℤ the class of ⟨1⟩ has infinite order (signature).

sources.match: Defines strictly metabolic objects and the Witt group W(Proj(R);Q), notes it is the classical Witt group for abelian-group-valued Q, and proves W(Proj(R);Q) ≅ L^{0,0}_0(R;Q) by showing strict metabolicity is the same as having an allowed Lagrangian.

nodes.title: Strictly metabolic 1-quadratic forms are hyperbolic
nodes.statement: Let Q be 1-quadratic, P finitely generated projective and (P,q) strictly metabolic with strict Lagrangian L → P (so fib(L → P) ≃ DL[−1] and P ≅ L ⊕ DL). Then (P,q) ≃ hyp(L).
hypotheses: Q 1-quadratic (e.g. Q^ge_M, Q^gq_M, Q^q_M).
proofSteps: By the algebraic Thom isomorphism (Calmès et al. I, Corollary 2.4.6), Poincaré structures on L → P in Met(D^p(R),Q) correspond to points of ΩQ(DL[−1]).
As Q is 1-quadratic, HK.2/shifted-projective-connectivity (or Remark 1.1.3 directly) shows this space is connected, so the metabolic object is equivalent to the hyperbolic one on L.
acceptance: Over 𝔽₂ with Q^s (not 1-quadratic) the strictly metabolic plane with b(v,v) = 0, b(u,u) = 1 is not hyperbolic, so the hypothesis is needed.
This recovers the classical fact that a strictly metabolic quadratic form on a projective module is hyperbolic.

sources.match: Uses the algebraic Thom isomorphism and connectedness of the space of shifted forms for a 1-quadratic structure to show strictly metabolic objects are hyperbolic.
The algebraic Thom isomorphism identifying Poincaré objects of the metabolic category over a fixed arrow with shifted forms on its fibre.

nodes.title: Widening the Lagrangian bound by one changes nothing
nodes.statement: For any M-compatible Poincaré structure Q on D^p(R), any n ∈ ℤ and a ≥ 0 with a + n even, the canonical map L^{a,a}_n(R;Q) → L^{a,a+1}_n(R;Q) is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: Q compatible with an invertible M, as in HK.3/bounded-l-monoids; no quadraticity or symmetry hypothesis.
proofSteps: Surjectivity: both are quotients of the same monoid π₀Pn^a_n.

Injectivity reduces to: if (L → X) ∈ π₀M^{a,a+1}_n then X is zero in L^{a,a}_n. Write k = (−n−a)/2; L is represented in [k−1, k+a], so there is a fibre sequence L″ → L → L′ with L″ = P[k−1] for P projective and L′ k-connective.

View L″ → L as a morphism in Met(D^p(R),Q) with source L″ → L″; since Q^met of an identity arrow is contractible it refines canonically to a surgery datum. Surgery gives a Lagrangian L′ → X′ in M^{a,a}_n with X′ still k-connective.

Since L″ → X is null (X is k-connective), the datum splits as the trivial datum on X plus a datum L″ → 0 given by a loop in Ω^nQ(L″); so X′ ≃ X ⊕ Z where Z carries the Lagrangian Ω^{n+1}DL″ = (DP)[−n−k], which is k-connective. Hence [X] = [X′] = 0 in L^{a,a}_n.
acceptance: (n,a) = (0,0): L^{0,0}_0 ≅ L^{0,1}_0, which with HK.3/strictly-metabolic-witt identifies the Witt group with L^{0,1}_0.

sources.match: Proves that L^{a,a}_n → L^{a,a+1}_n is an isomorphism for every Poincaré structure by splitting off a bottom-degree projective from a width a+1 Lagrangian and performing surgery in the metabolic category.

nodes.title: Surgery for m-quadratic Poincaré structures
nodes.statement: Let Q be an m-quadratic Poincaré structure on D^p(R), n ∈ ℤ, and a, b ≥ 0 with b ≥ a − 1 and n + a, n + 1 + b even. (i) If a ≥ n − 2m, every Poincaré object of (D^p(R),Q[−n]) is cobordant to a ((−n−a)/2)-connective one. (ii) If b ≥ n − 2m + 1, every Lagrangian L → X of a ((−n−a)/2)-connective Poincaré object is cobordant relative to X to a Lagrangian L′ → X with L′ and fib(L′ → X) both ((−n−1−b)/2)-connective. If both inequalities hold, L^{a,b}_n(R;Q) is a group, L^{a,b}_n(R;Q) → L_n(R;Q) is an isomorphism, and π₀M^{a,b}_n → π₀Pn^a_n → L^{a,b}_n is exact in the middle. The objects in (i) are concentrated in [(−n−a)/2, (−n+a)/2] and the Lagrangians in (ii) in [(−n−1−b)/2, (−n−1+b)/2].
hypotheses: Q M-compatible and m-quadratic; parities n + a and n + 1 + b even; a, b ≥ 0.
proofSteps: (i) If X is k-connective with k < (−n−a)/2, choose a projective P and P[k] → X onto on H_k (HK.2/width-criterion).

By HK.2/shifted-projective-connectivity, Q(P[k]) is min(−2k, m−k)-connective and min(−2k, m−k) > min(n+a, (2m+n+a)/2) ≥ n, so Ω^{∞+n}Q(P[k]) is connected and q restricts to zero on P[k]: this is a surgery datum.
Surgery (GN §6.8a) gives X′ = fib(X/P[k] → D(P)[−k−n]); since −k−n > k+1 (from −2k−1 > n+a ≥ n), X′ is (k+1)-connective. Induct.

(ii) If N = fib(L → X) is l-connective with l < (−n−1−b)/2, choose P[l] → N onto on H_l; Q^met(P[l] → 0) ≃ ΩQ(P[l]) is (n+1)-connective by the same estimate with n+1+b, so this is a Lagrangian surgery datum (HK.3/lagrangian-surgery). The new fibre N′ fits into N′ → N/P[l] → D(P)[−l−n−1] and is (l+1)-connective. Induct; L′ inherits the bound because b ≥ a − 1.
The diagonal Lagrangian and (ii) make L^{a,b}_n a group; (i) gives surjectivity and (ii) injectivity onto L_n(R;Q); (ii) also gives exactness in the middle.
acceptance: Numerical core: for integers with n + a even, a ≥ n − 2m, a ≥ 0 and 2k < −n − a, one has n < −2k and n < m − k (checked by omega in Suggested.lean).
For Q^q_M (m arbitrary) every n is in range.

sources.locator: Proposition 1.2.6 and Remark 1.2.7, p. 16; proof pp. 17–18; Remark 1.2.11, p. 18
sources.match: Proves that for an m-quadratic structure Poincaré objects and Lagrangians can be made connective by surgery along projectives in the stated ranges, that L^{a,b}_n is then a group isomorphic to L_n, gives the concentration intervals, and notes exactness in the middle.

nodes.title: Representatives for quadratic L-groups
nodes.statement: Q^q_M is m-quadratic for every m. For n = 2k, every class of L^q_n(R;M) is represented by a Poincaré object concentrated in degree −k, which is zero iff it has a Lagrangian concentrated in degrees [−k−1,−k]. For n = 2k+1, every class is represented in degrees [−k−1,−k] and is zero iff it has a Lagrangian concentrated in degree −k−1. The same holds for any m-quadratic Q provided n ≤ 2m (surgery below the middle dimension).
hypotheses: Q = Q^q_M, or Q m-quadratic with n ≤ 2m.
proofSteps: Apply HK.4/quadratic-surgery with (a,b) = (0,1) for n even and (1,0) for n odd; read the intervals from HK.3/bounded-l-monoids.
acceptance: For R = ℤ, L^q_0(ℤ) = ℤ is generated by the E₈ form in degree 0 (GN §6.10a).

sources.match: Applies quadratic surgery with (a,b) = (0,1) and (1,0) to describe representatives and null-cobordisms for quadratic L-groups, and notes the same for m-quadratic structures with n ≤ 2m.

nodes.title: Representatives for genuine symmetric L-groups
nodes.statement: For every n ≥ 0, every class of L^gs_n(R;M) is represented by a Poincaré object concentrated in degrees [−n,0], and such an object is zero iff it has a Lagrangian concentrated in degrees [−n−1,0]. Equivalently L^{n,n+1}_n(R;Q^gs_M) → L^gs_n(R;M) is an isomorphism.
proofSteps: Q^gs_M is 0-quadratic (HK.2/genuine-family-bounds); apply HK.4/quadratic-surgery with m = 0, (a,b) = (n,n+1): a = n ≥ n, b = n+1 ≥ n+1, and n + a, n + 1 + b are even.
acceptance: n = 0: classes are symmetric forms on projective modules and Lagrangians are complexes in [−1,0].

sources.match: States that genuine symmetric L-classes in degree n ≥ 0 are represented in [−n,0] with null-cobordisms in [−n−1,0], i.e. L^{n,n+1}_n(R;Q^gs_M) ≅ L^gs_n(R;M), from quadratic surgery with m = 0.

nodes.title: Quadratic L-theory agrees with an m-quadratic flavour in low degrees
nodes.statement: If Q is m-quadratic (for instance Q = Q^{≥m}_M), the map L^q_n(R;M) = L_n(R;Q^q_M) → L_n(R;Q) is an isomorphism for n ≤ 2m − 3 and surjective for n = 2m − 2. The range is essentially optimal: for R = ℤ and m = 0, ℤ/2 ≅ L^q_{−2}(ℤ) → L^gs_{−2}(ℤ) = 0 is not injective.
hypotheses: Q M-compatible and m-quadratic.
proofSteps: For n ≤ 2m − 2 pick a ∈ {0,1} with n + a even; then a ≥ n − 2m, so both sides are represented by ((−n−a)/2)-connective objects (HK.4/quadratic-surgery (i)).
On such X, DX ≃ ΣⁿX is ((n−a)/2)-connective, so the cofibre of Q^q_M(X) → Q(X) is (m + (n−a)/2)-connective and m + (n−a)/2 ≥ n + 1; hence Q^q_M(X) → Q(X) is onto on π_n: surjectivity.

For n ≤ 2m − 3 pick b ∈ {0,1} with n + 1 + b even; by (ii) a Lagrangian may be taken with L and its fibre ((−n−1−b)/2)-connective; then DL ≃ Σ^{n+1}N is ((n+1−b)/2)-connective and the cofibre on L is (2m+n+1−b)/2 ≥ n + 2 connective, so Q^q_M(L) → Q(L) is bijective on π_n and onto on π_{n+1}: the Lagrangian refines to a Q^q_M-Lagrangian: injectivity.
The printed proof ends with 'n ≤ 2n − 3', which should read 'n ≤ 2m − 3' (sourceIssues E1).
acceptance: Q = Q^gs_M (m = 0): L^q_n ≅ L^gs_n for n ≤ −3 and onto for n = −2.
Q = Q^gq_M (m = 2): L^q_n ≅ L^gq_n for n ≤ 1 (compare GN §6.10a over ℤ).

sources.match: Proves that quadratic L-theory maps isomorphically to the L-theory of an m-quadratic structure for n ≤ 2m − 3 and surjectively for n = 2m − 2, and shows the range cannot be improved using L^q_{−2}(ℤ) = ℤ/2 and L^gs_{−2}(ℤ) = 0.

nodes.title: Degree-zero L-groups are classical Witt groups
nodes.statement: If Q is 0-quadratic, W(Proj(R);Q) → L₀(R;Q) is an isomorphism. Consequently (i) L^gs_0(R;M) is the Witt group of M-valued symmetric forms over R, (ii) L^ge_0(R;M) the Witt group of M-valued even forms, and (iii) L₀(R;Q^{≥m}_M) the Witt group of M-valued quadratic forms for every m ≥ 2. Combined with L^gs_{−2k}(R;M((−1)^k)) ≅ L₀(R;Q^{≥k}_M) (HK.1/bordism-invariant-periodicity), every even non-positive genuine symmetric L-group is a Witt group of symmetric (k = 0), even (k = 1) or quadratic (k ≥ 2) forms; the odd groups in degrees ≤ 1 have analogous descriptions by symmetric, even and quadratic formations, which the source leaves to the reader.
hypotheses: Q 0-quadratic (every Q^{≥m}_M with m ≥ 0).
proofSteps: W(Proj(R);Q) ≅ L^{0,0}_0(R;Q) (HK.3/strictly-metabolic-witt), L^{0,0}_0 ≅ L^{0,1}_0 (HK.3/widen-lagrangian-bound) and L^{0,1}_0 ≅ L₀ (HK.4/quadratic-surgery with m = 0, (a,b) = (0,1)).
On P[0] the values of Q^{≥2}, Q^{≥1}, Q^{≥0} are the groups of quadratic, even and symmetric forms (GN §6.8a; Calmès et al. I, Proposition 4.2.22): this gives (i)–(iii) for m = 0, 1, 2.
For m > 2, L^q_0 → L₀(Q^{≥m}) is an isomorphism by HK.4/quadratic-low-degree-comparison (0 ≤ 2m − 3), reducing to m = 2.
Shift with HK.1/bordism-invariant-periodicity for the negative even degrees.
acceptance: L^gs_0(𝔽₂) = W(𝔽₂) = ℤ/2 generated by ⟨1⟩; L^ge_0(𝔽₂) = 0 because even forms in characteristic 2 are alternating and hence metabolic.
L^gs_0(ℤ) = ℤ by signature and L₀(ℤ;Q^gq) = ℤ by signature/8 (E₈).

sources.locator: Proposition 1.2.15, Corollary 1.2.16, p. 19, and Remark 1.2.17, p. 20
sources.match: Proves W(Proj(R);Q) ≅ L₀(R;Q) for 0-quadratic Q, identifies the degree-zero genuine L-groups with Witt groups of symmetric, even and quadratic forms, and describes the even non-positive genuine symmetric L-groups through periodicity, leaving the odd formation description to the reader.
Identifies Q^{≥2}, Q^{≥1}, Q^{≥0} with the non-abelian derived functors of quadratic, even and symmetric forms on projectives.

nodes.title: Free and K₀-controlled variants
nodes.statement: Let 𝒞 be a full subcategory with D^f(R) ⊆ 𝒞 ⊆ D^p(R) closed under the duality, for instance the objects whose class in K₀(R) lies in a given involution-closed subgroup. If M is free (needed for 𝒞 = D^f(R)), the results of HK.4/quadratic-surgery, HK.4/genuine-symmetric-representatives and HK.4/witt-group-computes-L0 hold for (𝒞,Q|_𝒞), with projective modules replaced by stably free (respectively stably-𝒞) ones. For example, for 0-quadratic Q every element of L_n(D^f(R),Q), n ≥ 0, is represented by a Poincaré form on a complex of stably free modules in degrees [−n,0], vanishing iff it has a Lagrangian of stably free modules in degrees [−n−1,0], and L₀(D^f(R),Q) is the Witt group of stably free Poincaré objects.
hypotheses: 𝒞 closed under duality, containing D^f(R); M free when free complexes are used.
proofSteps: In the proof of quadratic surgery choose P free; the surgery then stays in D^f(R) (or in 𝒞).
The connectivity bounds translate into stably free representability by the refinement in HK.2/width-criterion.
Run the proof of HK.4/witt-group-computes-L0 verbatim with stably free modules.
acceptance: 𝒞 = D^p(R) recovers the uncontrolled statements.
For R a principal ideal domain, stably free = free and D^f(R) = D^p(R).

sources.match: Explains that the surgery results apply to finite free complexes when M is free, with stably free representatives, and to any intermediate duality-closed subcategory such as a K₀-controlled one.

nodes.title: Ranicki's short symmetric L-groups
nodes.statement: Let Ch^b(Proj(R)) be bounded chain complexes of finitely generated projective left R-modules, C n-dimensional if C_i = 0 for i ∉ [0,n], and DC the dual complex Hom_R(C,M) with (DC)_i = D(C_{−i}). For n ≥ 0, an n-dimensional (symmetric) Poincaré complex is (C,q) with C n-dimensional and q ∈ H_n(Hom_R(DC,C)^{hC₂}) (homotopy fixed points computed with the standard free resolution of ℤ over ℤ[C₂]) whose image in H_n(Hom_R(DC,C)) = [DC[n],C] is an isomorphism in the homotopy category. An (n+1)-dimensional Poincaré pair is (f : C → C′, η) with C n-dimensional, C′ (n+1)-dimensional and η ∈ H_n(fib[Hom_R(DC,C) → Hom_R(DC′,C′)]^{hC₂}) whose images in [DC[n],C] and [cof(DC′ → DC)[n],C′] are isomorphisms. A Poincaré complex arising as the boundary of a pair is null-cobordant; (C,q), (C′,q′) are cobordant if (C ⊕ C′, q ⊕ −q′) is null-cobordant. The cobordism classes form an abelian group L^short_n(R;M) under ⊕ with −(C,q) = (C,−q); quasi-isomorphic complexes are cobordant, and L^short_n is the cokernel of M^short_n(R) → Pn^short_n(R) in commutative monoids. For negative n, Ranicki puts L^short_n(R;M) := L^{short,ev}_{n+2}(R;−M) for n = −2, −1 and L^short_n(R;M) := L^q_n(R;M) for n ≤ −3, where L^{short,ev}_n is the cobordism group of even complexes: those whose Wu class v₀(q) : H^n(C) → Ĥ^0(C₂;M) vanishes, with even pairs defined by the vanishing of the relative Wu class on H^{n+1}(f).
hypotheses: M any invertible ℤ-module with involution (Ranicki states the definition for M = R(ε); only the induced duality on complexes is used).
Here H^n(C) = H_{−n}(DC) is the cohomology of C.
proofSteps: Ranicki's definitions (Ranicki 1980, §1 and §3) use only the duality C ↦ DC on complexes and the C₂-action on Hom_R(DC,C), so they extend from R(ε) to any invertible M.

A quasi-isomorphism f : C → C′ with f_*q = q′ gives a Poincaré pair with boundary C ⊕ C′, written (id,f) : C → C ⊕ C′ in the Lagrangian convention of Remark 1.2.21, witnessing the cobordism; so quasi-isomorphism is finer than cobordism and the monoid presentation follows.
acceptance: L^short_0(R;M) is the Witt group of M-valued symmetric forms on projectives (compare HK.4/witt-group-computes-L0).
These complexes are not SymplecticReidemeisterTorsionModSquares RT.0's strict symmetric pairings C ⊗ C → R[−n]: Ranicki's structure is a class in homotopy fixed points of Hom_R(DC,C).

nodes.title: Ranicki's groups are bounded L-groups of the symmetric structure
nodes.statement: Let I_n ⊆ Ch^b(Proj(R)) be the n-dimensional complexes with quasi-isomorphisms and J_{[0,n]} ⊆ D^p(R)^≃ the perfect modules representable in degrees [0,n]. Localisation restricts to π : I_n → J_{[0,n]}, an equivalence on homotopy categories, and there are natural isomorphisms H_n(Hom_R(DC,C)^{hC₂}) ≅ π_n(Hom_R(DπC,πC)^{hC₂}) ≅ π₀Ω^nQ^s_M(πDC). Sending (C,q) to the component of (πDC, ρ(q)) is a monoid isomorphism Pn^short_n(R) ≅ π₀Pn^n_n(R;Q^s_M), compatible with pairs, and induces L^short_n(R;M) ≅ L^{n,n+1}_n(R;Q^s_M) for n ≥ 0.
proofSteps: The localisation Ch^b(Proj(R)) → D^p(R) identifies homotopy classes of maps and preserves sums; complexes in [0,n] go to objects representable in [0,n] (HK.2/width-criterion), and DπC is then concentrated in [−n,0], matching the bounds of Pn^n_n.
The Hom complex computes the mapping spectrum (GN §6.8a `perfectDerivedHom`) and the explicit resolution computes homotopy fixed points, giving ρ.

Applying the same construction to arrow categories gives M^short_n(R) → π₀M^{n,n+1}_n(R;Q^s_M) compatibly; every arrow of D^p(R) lifts to a chain map, which gives surjectivity, hence an isomorphism of quotients.
acceptance: n = 0: both sides are Witt groups of symmetric forms on projectives (HK.3/strictly-metabolic-witt).

nodes.title: Symmetric and r-symmetric forms agree in bounded width
nodes.statement: Let Q be r-symmetric and a, b, n as in HK.3/bounded-l-monoids with a ≤ n + 2r − 4 and b ≤ n + 2r − 3. Then L^{a,b}_n(R;Q) → L^{a,b}_n(R;Q^s_M) is an isomorphism. In particular, Q^gs_M being 2-symmetric, L^{n,n+1}_n(R;Q^gs_M) ≅ L^{n,n+1}_n(R;Q^s_M) for every n ≥ 0.
hypotheses: Q M-compatible and r-symmetric.
proofSteps: It suffices that π₀Pn^a_n(R;Q) → π₀Pn^a_n(R;Q^s_M) and π₀M^{a,b}_n(R;Q) → π₀M^{a,b}_n(R;Q^s_M) are bijections.

For ((−n−a)/2)-connective X the fibre of Q(X) → Q^s_M(X) is (−r + (n+a)/2)-truncated (HK.2/r-symmetric-m-quadratic), and −r + (n+a)/2 ≤ n − 2 because a ≤ n + 2r − 4; a map whose fibre is (n−2)-truncated induces an equivalence on Ω^{∞+n}.

For pairs, the map Q^met(L → X) → Q^{s,met}(L → X) must have (n−2)-truncated fibre; the top map of the square (on X) is (n−2)-truncated as above and the bottom map (on L, which is ⌈(−n−1−b)/2⌉-connective) is (n−1)-truncated by b ≤ n + 2r − 3, so the total fibre is (n−2)-truncated.

sources.match: Proves that for an r-symmetric structure the bounded L-monoids agree with those of the symmetric structure when a ≤ n + 2r − 4 and b ≤ n + 2r − 3, by truncatedness estimates on forms and on metabolic forms, and specialises to the genuine symmetric structure.

nodes.title: Ranicki's even L-groups are genuine even L-groups
nodes.statement: For n ≥ 0, sending an n-dimensional even Poincaré complex (C,φ) to (DC, ρ(φ)) induces isomorphisms L^{short,ev}_n(R;M) ≅ L^{n,n+1}_n(R;Q^ge_M) ≅ L^ge_n(R;M). The refinement of a genuine symmetric to a genuine even structure is controlled by the fibre sequence Ω^nQ^ge(X) → Ω^nQ^gs(X) → Hom_R(X, Ĥ^0(C₂;M)[−n]), whose last term has Ω^∞ ≃ Hom_R(H_{−n}(X), Ĥ^0(C₂;M)); the image of the symmetric structure there is Ranicki's Wu class v₀(φ).
hypotheses: n ≥ 0; M invertible.
proofSteps: By HK.4/short-to-bounded and HK.4/genuine-symmetric-bounded-agreement, (C,φ) gives a class in L^{n,n+1}_n(R;Q^gs_M) represented by X = DC.

By the defining pullbacks (GN §6.8a) the cofibre of Q^ge_M → Q^gs_M at X is Hom_R(X, cofib(τ_{≥1}HM^{tC₂} → τ_{≥0}HM^{tC₂})) = Hom_R(X, HĤ^0(C₂;M)); after Ω^n this is the displayed fibre sequence. Tracing the definitions, the image of the symmetric structure is Ranicki's Wu class v₀(φ), which vanishes for even complexes, so the class refines canonically to Q^ge_M; the same holds for even pairs, and reversing the argument gives the inverse map.
L^{n,n+1}_n(R;Q^ge_M) ≅ L^ge_n(R;M) by HK.4/quadratic-surgery since Q^ge_M is 1-quadratic (a = n ≥ n − 2, b = n + 1 ≥ n − 1).
acceptance: n = 0: L^{short,ev}_0 is the Witt group of even forms, matching HK.4/witt-group-computes-L0 (ii).

sources.match: Constructs the map from Ranicki's short even L-groups to L^{n,n+1}_n(R;Q^ge_M) using the fibre sequence from Q^ge to Q^gs with cofibre Hom_R(X, Ĥ^0(C₂;M)[−n]) and the vanishing of the Wu class, shows it is an isomorphism, and compares with L^ge_n by surgery.

nodes.title: Theorem 5: Ranicki's symmetric L-groups are the genuine symmetric L-groups
nodes.statement: For every ring R, invertible ℤ-module with involution M over R and every n ∈ ℤ there is a natural isomorphism L^short_n(R;M) ≅ L^gs_n(R;M). In particular L^short(R;M) := τ_{≥0}L^gs(R;M) is a connective spectrum whose homotopy groups are Ranicki's original symmetric L-groups, and Ranicki's negative groups are L^gs_n(R;M) = L^ev_{n+2}(R;−M) for n = −2, −1 and L^q_n(R;M) for n ≤ −3.
hypotheses: No hypothesis on R or on 2.
proofSteps: n ≥ 0: compose L^short_n ≅ L^{n,n+1}_n(R;Q^s_M) (HK.4/short-to-bounded) ≅ L^{n,n+1}_n(R;Q^gs_M) (HK.4/genuine-symmetric-bounded-agreement) ≅ L^gs_n(R;M) (HK.4/genuine-symmetric-representatives).
n ≤ −3: L^q_n ≅ L^gs_n by HK.4/quadratic-low-degree-comparison with m = 0, matching Ranicki's definition.
n = −2, −1: L^gs_n(R;M) ≅ L^ge_{n+2}(R;−M) by HK.1/bordism-invariant-periodicity, and L^ge_{n+2}(R;−M) ≅ L^{short,ev}_{n+2}(R;−M) by HK.4/short-even-comparison.
acceptance: L^gs_n(ℤ) for n = 0, 1 is ℤ (signature) and ℤ/2 (de Rham invariant), as in GN §6.10a.

nodes.title: Ranicki's quadratic L-groups and a warning
nodes.statement: For n ≥ 0, Ranicki's n-th quadratic L-group (quadratic Poincaré complexes of dimension n) coincides with L^{n,n+1}_n(R;Q^q_M) and hence with L^q_n(R;M); these are Wall's quadratic L-groups, the recipients of surgery obstructions. They are not L^gq_n(R;M): by periodicity L^gq_n(R;M) ≅ L^gs_{n−4}(R;M).
proofSteps: Run HK.4/short-to-bounded with homotopy orbits in place of fixed points to get Ranicki's quadratic group ≅ L^{n,n+1}_n(R;Q^q_M), then HK.4/quadratic-surgery (Q^q_M is m-quadratic for all m).
Σ⁴L^gs ≃ L^gq by HK.1/bordism-invariant-periodicity.
acceptance: Over ℤ, L^q_2(ℤ) = ℤ/2 (Arf invariant) whereas L^gq_2(ℤ) ≅ L^gs_{−2}(ℤ) = 0, so Ranicki's (Wall's) quadratic L-groups are not the genuine quadratic ones.

sources.match: Identifies Ranicki's quadratic L-groups with L^q_n via the same argument, notes they are Wall's groups, and warns they differ from L^gq_n, which is a four-fold shift of L^gs.

nodes.title: Poincaré structures on compact modules over a connective ring spectrum
nodes.statement: Let A be a connective E₁-ring (a connective associative algebra in spectra, ⊗ over 𝕊) and Mod^ω_A its stable ∞-category of compact left modules; Proj(A) ⊆ Mod^ω_A are the retracts of A^n. Let M be an invertible module with involution over A (Calmès et al. I, Definition 3.1.1) that is projective in either A-module structure, so the duality D = hom_A(−,M) preserves Proj(A). The quadratic and symmetric structures are Q^q_M(X) = hom_{A⊗A}(X⊗X,M)_{hC₂} and Q^s_M(X) = hom_{A⊗A}(X⊗X,M)^{hC₂}; the genuine symmetric structure Q^gs_M is the pullback of Q^s_M(X) → hom_A(X,M^{tC₂}) along hom_A(X,τ_{≥0}M^{tC₂}); for a connective E∞-ring B the Tate structure Q^t_B is the pullback of Q^s_B(Y) → hom_B(Y,B^{tC₂}) along the Tate-valued Frobenius hom_B(Y,B) → hom_B(Y,B^{tC₂}); and on Mod^ω_𝕊 the universal structure Q^u has linear part hom(−,𝕊) and agrees with Q^t_𝕊. An A-module is k-connective if its underlying spectrum is; Q is m-quadratic if the cofibre of Q^q_M → Q is m-connective on A, equivalently on Proj(A); Λ_Q denotes the linear part. Pn^a_n, M^{a,b}_n and L^{a,b}_n(A;Q) are defined verbatim from HK.3/bounded-l-monoids. The maps A → π₀A and M → π₀M induce Poincaré functors (Mod^ω_A, Q^α_M) → (Mod^ω_{π₀A}, Q^α_{π₀M}) for α = q, gs, and B → π₀B induces one for Q^t.
hypotheses: A connective E₁-ring; M projective in both module structures; B connective E∞ for Q^t.
proofSteps: Mod^ω_A and its tensor products are EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:abstract/module-objects and E5:presentability/compact-objects; compact A-modules form a small stable idempotent-complete category (GeneralAlgebraicKTheoryPartII KII.0/ring-k-theory).

The formulas define Poincaré structures with duality hom_A(−,M) by Calmès et al. I, §3 (Lemma 3.2.5, Construction 3.2.6, Examples 3.2.8 and 3.2.12); the pullback along a connective cover of the Tate term is the genuine construction of GN §6.8a over a ring spectrum.
The universal structure is Calmès et al. I, Example 1.2.15; its linear part is hom(−,𝕊), and the Frobenius 𝕊 → 𝕊^{tC₂} identifies it with Q^t_𝕊.
Base change along A → π₀A preserves compact modules and the forms, giving the Poincaré functors.
acceptance: For A = Hℤ discrete, Mod^ω_A ≃ D^p(ℤ) and the structures are those of GN §6.8a.

nodes.title: Compact connective modules and recognition of projectives
nodes.statement: Let A be a connective E₁-ring. If X ∈ Mod^ω_A is connective then π₀X is finitely presented over π₀A, so there is A^n → X with 1-connective cofibre. If X is projective so is DX and both are connective; conversely if X and DX are connective then X is projective, and more generally X is the k-fold suspension of a projective iff X is k-connective and DX is (−k)-connective. If X is connective and DX is (−1)-connective, X is the cofibre of a map P → Q of projectives; more generally X is k-connective with DX (−k−1)-connective iff X is the k-fold suspension of such a cofibre.
hypotheses: A connective; M projective in both structures.
proofSteps: π₀A ⊗_A X is connective and perfect over the discrete ring π₀A with the same π₀; over a discrete ring connective perfect modules are finite complexes of projectives in non-negative degrees (HK.2/width-criterion), so π₀ is finitely presented.
Given A^n → X → Y with Y 1-connective, invertibility of M gives hom_A(X,Y) ≃ hom_A(M,Y) ⊗_A DX, which is 1-connective when DX is connective; so X → Y is null and A^n → X splits up to homotopy.
For the two-term case, P := ΩY is connective with D_MP the cofibre of D_MX → M^n, hence connective, so P is projective by the first case and X = cofib(P → A^n).
acceptance: For A discrete these reduce to HK.2/width-criterion with intervals [k,k] and [k,k+1].

sources.match: Proves π₀ of a compact connective module is finitely presented and characterises projectives and two-term objects by connectivity of X and its dual, using invertibility of M.

nodes.title: Quadratic surgery over connective ring spectra
nodes.statement: Let Q be an m-quadratic Poincaré structure on Mod^ω_A, n ∈ ℤ, and a, b ≥ 0 with b ≥ a − 1 and n + a, n + 1 + b even. (i) If a ≥ n − 2m, every Poincaré object of (Mod^ω_A, Q[−n]) is cobordant to a ((−n−a)/2)-connective one. (ii) If b ≥ n − 2m + 1, every Lagrangian L → X of such an object is cobordant relative to X to one with L′ and fib(L′ → X) both ((−n−1−b)/2)-connective. If both hold, L^{a,b}_n(A;Q) is a group and L^{a,b}_n(A;Q) → L_n(A;Q) is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: Setting of HK.5/ring-spectrum-setting; P[k] means Σ^kP.
proofSteps: Lemma HK.2/shifted-projective-connectivity holds verbatim for Σ^kP with P ∈ Proj(A).
The only use of discreteness in HK.4/quadratic-surgery is the existence of P[k] → X with (k+1)-connective cofibre for k-connective X; this is HK.5/compact-connective-pi0.
The rest of the proof of HK.4/quadratic-surgery runs verbatim.
acceptance: For A = HR this is HK.4/quadratic-surgery.

nodes.title: Lifting projectives along a π₀-isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let f : A → B be a map of connective E₁-rings inducing an isomorphism π₀A → π₀B (for instance a 1-connective map). Then extension of scalars B ⊗_A − : Proj(A) → Proj(B) induces an equivalence of homotopy categories. Hence projective B-modules and maps between them lift, uniquely up to homotopy, to projective A-modules, and perfect B-modules presented as (co)fibres of maps of projectives lift to perfect A-modules of the same kind.
hypotheses: A, B connective E₁-rings; π₀f an isomorphism.
proofSteps: Full faithfulness: for P free, Ext⁰_A(P,Q) is a product of copies of π₀Q and Ext⁰_B is a product of copies of π₀(B ⊗_A Q) ≅ Tor^{π₀A}_0(π₀B, π₀Q) ≅ π₀Q.
Essential surjectivity: a projective B-module is a retract of B^n; lift the idempotent on π₀ and realise it on A^n (Lurie, HA, Corollary 7.2.2.19 and the preceding Proposition 7.2.2.18).
Lifting (co)fibres of maps of projectives follows by lifting the map.
acceptance: For A = 𝕊, B = Hℤ: π₀ is ℤ in both; free 𝕊-modules 𝕊^n lift ℤ^n and maps ℤ^n → ℤ^m (integer matrices) lift to 𝕊^n → 𝕊^m.

sources.match: Proves that base change along a map of connective E₁-rings inducing an isomorphism on π₀ induces an equivalence of homotopy categories of projective modules.
Records this fact and its consequences for lifting projectives, maps and two-term perfect modules, for use in Proposition 1.2.29.

nodes.title: Comparison of L-groups along a 1-connective map
nodes.statement: Fix m, p ∈ ℤ. Let f : A → B be a 1-connective map of connective ring spectra, M and N projective invertible modules with involution over A and B, and Q_M, Q_N Poincaré structures on Mod^ω_A and Mod^ω_B that are m-quadratic with respect to M and N. Suppose f_! refines to a Poincaré functor (Mod^ω_A,Q_M) → (Mod^ω_B,Q_N) whose map on bilinear parts M = B_{Q_M}(A,A) → B_{Q_N}(B,B) = N is 1-connective and whose map on linear parts Λ_{Q_M}(A) → Λ_{Q_N}(B) is p-connective. Then L_n(A;Q_M) → L_n(B;Q_N) is an isomorphism for n ≤ min(2p−1, 2m) and surjective for n = min(2p, 2m+1).
hypotheses: f 1-connective (cofibre 1-connective on underlying spectra).
proofSteps: For X with DX r-connective, compare the cofibre sequences Q^q(X) → Q(X) → Λ_Q(X) for M and N: the map on the quadratic terms is (2r+1)-connective (bilinear part 1-connective) and on linear terms (r+p)-connective; hence Q_M(X) → Q_N(f_!X) is min(2r+1, r+p)-connective.

Surjectivity for n ≤ min(2p, 2m+1): with a ∈ {0,1}, n + a even, classes on both sides are represented by ((−n−a)/2)-connective objects (HK.5/ring-spectrum-surgery); such B-objects are shifted projectives or two-term objects (HK.5/compact-connective-pi0) and lift to A (HK.5/lifting-projectives); for them DX is r = (n−a)/2 ≤ p connective and the form map is onto on π_n.

Injectivity for n ≤ min(2p−1, 2m): with b ∈ {0,1}, n + 1 + b even, a Lagrangian over B may be taken with L and its fibre ((−n−1−b)/2)-connective; write L = fib(U → V) with U, V projective shifts, factor L → f_!X through f_!Q, lift U → V and the map to Q, and check that Q_M(L′) → Q_N(f_!L′) is injective on π_n and onto on π_{n+1}, which follows from the estimate with r′ = (n+1−b)/2.
acceptance: f = id, Q_M = Q^q_M: recovers HK.4/quadratic-low-degree-comparison over A (p = m − 1 effectively, via Corollary 1.2.30).
For Q^q structures (Λ = 0 on both sides, p = ∞) and m = ∞ the map is an isomorphism in all degrees.

sources.match: States and proves that a Poincaré refinement of base change along a 1-connective map, with 1-connective bilinear and p-connective linear comparison, induces isomorphisms on L_n for n ≤ min(2p−1,2m) and a surjection for n = min(2p,2m+1).

nodes.title: Quadratic comparison over a ring spectrum and the sphere
nodes.statement: If Q_M on Mod^ω_A is m-quadratic with respect to a projective invertible M, then L^q_n(A;M) → L_n(A;Q_M) is an isomorphism for n ≤ 2m − 3 and surjective for n = 2m − 2. For the sphere: Q^u on Mod^ω_𝕊 is 0-quadratic, so L^q_n(𝕊) → L^u_n(𝕊) is an isomorphism for n ≤ −3; and since 𝕊^{tC₂} is the 2-completed sphere, which is connective by Lin's theorem, Q^s on Mod^ω_𝕊 is also 0-quadratic and L^q_n(𝕊) → L^s_n(𝕊) is an isomorphism for n ≤ −3.

Λ_{Q^u}(𝕊) = 𝕊 is connective; Λ_{Q^s}(𝕊) = 𝕊^{tC₂} ≃ 𝕊^∧₂ is connective by Lin's theorem.

nodes.title: Comparison of the L-theory of a ring spectrum with that of its π₀
nodes.statement: Let A be a connective ring spectrum, M a projective invertible module with involution over A and B a connective E∞-ring. (i) L^q(A;M) → L^q(π₀A;π₀M) is an equivalence. (ii) L^t_n(B) → L^t_n(π₀B) is an isomorphism for n ≤ 0 and surjective for n = 1. (iii) L^gs_n(A;M) → L^gs_n(π₀A;π₀M) is an isomorphism for n ≤ −3 and surjective for n = −2; if the C₂-action on the spectrum underlying M is trivial, it is an isomorphism for n ≤ −1 and surjective for n = 0. The range in (iii) cannot be improved in general: for 𝕊^{2−2σ} ⊗ ko over ko, (𝕊^{2−2σ}⊗ko)^{tC₂} → ℤ^{tC₂} is not onto on π₀, since π_*(ko^{tC₂}) = ℤ^∧₂[u^{±1}] with |u| = 4 gives Σ²ko^{tC₂} trivial π₀ while ℤ^{tC₂} has π₀ = ℤ/2; 𝕊^{2−2σ} over 𝕊 is another example.
hypotheses: A → π₀A is 1-connective; M projective invertible.
proofSteps: Apply HK.5/connective-comparison to A → π₀A: for Q^q the linear parts vanish (p = ∞, m = ∞), giving (i) in all degrees.
For Q^t, B is 0-quadratic and the map on linear parts B → π₀B is 1-connective (p = 1): iso for n ≤ min(1, 0) = 0, onto for n = 1.

For Q^gs, 0-quadratic, the map on linear parts τ_{≥0}M^{tC₂} → τ_{≥0}(π₀M)^{tC₂} is (−1)-connective (p = −1): iso for n ≤ −3, onto for n = −2. With trivial action, M is a retract of M^{hC₂}, so π₀M^{hC₂} → π₀(π₀M)^{hC₂} = π₀M is onto, hence π₀ of the Tate map is onto and the linear map is 0-connective (p = 0): iso for n ≤ −1, onto n = 0.
For the counterexample use ko^{tC₂} from ChromaticHomotopyTheory CH.11 (real K-theory) and its Tate computation, recorded as an input.
acceptance: (i) is the algebraic π–π theorem of Lurie's notes, recovered here.
For A = 𝕊 and M = 𝕊 with trivial action, L^gs_n(𝕊) → L^gs_n(ℤ) is an isomorphism for n ≤ −1.

nodes.title: Coherent rings of finite global dimension
nodes.statement: A ring R is left-coherent if its finitely presented left modules form an abelian category, equivalently if every finitely generated left ideal is finitely presented. R has (left) global dimension ≤ d if every left R-module has a projective resolution of length ≤ d, i.e. every object of ModuleCat R has projective dimension ≤ d (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.HasProjectiveDimensionLE`). If R is coherent of global dimension ≤ d, every finitely presented module has a resolution of length ≤ d by finitely generated projectives. Noetherian rings and valuation rings are coherent; R has global dimension 0 iff it is semisimple; Dedekind domains have global dimension ≤ 1. Commutativity is not assumed; 'coherent' and 'global dimension' mean the left versions.
hypotheses: Left modules throughout.
proofSteps: The equivalence of the two coherence conditions is Chase's theorem; finitely presented modules are closed under kernels exactly when finitely generated ideals are finitely presented.

For finitely presented N, a resolution by finitely generated free modules exists by coherence (kernels of maps between finitely presented modules are finitely presented); truncating at stage d gives a projective d-th syzygy, since all Ext^{d+1} vanish.
Semisimple ⇔ every module projective ⇔ global dimension 0; for a Dedekind domain every submodule of a projective is projective (hereditary).
acceptance: ℤ and every field are coherent of global dimension ≤ 1, resp. 0.

nodes.title: The Postnikov t-structure on perfect complexes
nodes.statement: Let R be coherent of global dimension ≤ d. The connective cover and truncation functors of D(R) preserve perfect modules, so D^p(R) inherits the Postnikov t-structure with D^p(R)_{≥0} the 0-connective and D^p(R)_{≤0} the 0-truncated perfect modules. It is bounded, its heart consists of the finitely presented R-modules, and for an invertible M the duality D = Hom_R(−,M) satisfies D(D^p(R)_{≥0}) ⊆ D^p(R)_{≤0} and D(D^p(R)_{≤0}) ⊆ D^p(R)_{≥−d}.
hypotheses: R left-coherent of global dimension ≤ d; M invertible.
proofSteps: The lowest non-vanishing homology of a perfect complex is finitely presented by coherence; a finite resolution by finitely generated projectives (HK.6/coherent-global-dimension) shows truncations remain perfect.
The t-structure axioms are inherited from D(R) (Mathlib `DerivedCategory.TStructure.t` on the homotopy category, enhanced as in GeneralAlgebraicKTheoryPartII KII.3/bounded-t-structure).
D(D^p(R)_{≥0}) ⊆ D^p(R)_{≤0} is the one-sided width criterion (HK.2/width-criterion, Remark 1.1.7).
D(D^p(R)_{≤0}) ⊆ D^p(R)_{≥−d} follows from the universal coefficient spectral sequence for H_*Hom_R(X,M), since Ext^i_R(−,M) = 0 for i ≥ d+1.
acceptance: For R = ℤ (d = 1): D(ℤ/2[0]) = ℤ/2[−1] lies in D^p(ℤ)_{≥−1} and not in D^p(ℤ)_{≥0}.
For a field (d = 0) the duality exchanges the two halves and the heart is Proj(K).

nodes.title: r-symmetry and bounded L-monoids for a t-structured category
nodes.statement: Let C be a stable ∞-category with a t-structure (C_{≥0}, C_{≤0}) and a Poincaré structure Q with duality D. Q is r-symmetric if the fibre of Q(X) → Q^s_D(X) is (−r)-truncated for every X ∈ C_{≥0}, where Q^s_D(X) = hom_C(X,DX)^{hC₂}. For a, b ≥ −1 define Pn^a_n(C,Q), M^{a,b}_n(C,Q) and L^{a,b}_n(C,Q) as in HK.3/bounded-l-monoids, reading every connectivity condition in the given t-structure. L^{a,b}_n(C,Q) is a group if b ≥ a, and for C = D^p(R) with R coherent of finite global dimension and the Postnikov t-structure these agree with the earlier definitions.
hypotheses: C stable with a t-structure; Q Poincaré with duality D.
proofSteps: The definitions only use connectivity of objects, which makes sense in any t-structure.
The diagonal argument of HK.3/bounded-l-monoids for b ≥ a uses only the bounds on X.

For D^p(R), the Postnikov connectivity of a perfect module is the connectivity used in HK.3 (HK.6/perfect-postnikov-t-structure), and the two r-symmetry notions agree by HK.2/r-symmetric-m-quadratic (testing on P[0] is testing on the heart's projectives and propagating).
acceptance: For a field with the Postnikov t-structure, L^{0,0}_0(D^p(K),Q^s) is the Witt group of K.

nodes.title: Surgery for r-symmetric Poincaré structures
nodes.statement: Let C be a stable ∞-category with a t-structure, Q an r-symmetric Poincaré structure with duality D such that D(C_{≤0}) ⊆ C_{≥−d} for some d ≥ 0. Fix n ∈ ℤ and integers a ≥ d − 1, b ≥ d with b ≥ a, n + a even and a ≥ −n + 2d − 2r. Then (i) every Poincaré object of (C,Q[−n]) is cobordant to a ((−n−a)/2)-connective one; (ii) every Lagrangian L → X of a ((−n−a)/2)-connective Poincaré object is cobordant relative to X to a Lagrangian L′ → X with L′ ⌈(−n−1−b)/2⌉-connective and fib(L′ → X) ⌊(−n−1−b)/2⌋-connective. In particular L^{a,b}_n(C,Q) → L_n(C,Q) is an isomorphism and π₀M^{a,b}_n → π₀Pn^a_n → L^{a,b}_n is exact in the middle. The objects in (i) are concentrated in [(−n−a)/2, (−n+a)/2] and the Lagrangians in [⌈(−n−1−b)/2⌉, ⌈(−n−1+b)/2⌉]. (The source assumes the t-structure bounded; its proof does not use boundedness.)
hypotheses: Statement for a general C, not D^p(R) (corrected; sourceIssues E2).
The source assumes a bounded t-structure; the proof only uses truncations, exactness of the fibre of Q → Q^s_D and the duality bound.
proofSteps: (i) Put k = (−n−a−2)/2, W := Ω^nDτ_{≤k}X and f : W → Ω^nDX ≃ X dual to X → τ_{≤k}X.

W is (−n−k−d)-connective and DW ≃ Σ^nτ_{≤k}X is (n+k)-truncated, so Ω^n hom_C(W,DW)^{hC₂} is (n+2k+d)-truncated; by r-symmetry the fibre of Ω^nQ(W) → Ω^nQ^s_D(W) is (k+d−r)-truncated. Hence Ω^nQ(W) is max(n+2k+d, k+d−r)-truncated, and the hypotheses give max(n+2k+d, k+d−r) < 0.
So Ω^{∞+n}Q(W) ≃ * and q|_W is null: surgery along f gives X′ = cofib(W → τ_{≥k+1}X), which is (k+1)-connective because W is (k+1)-connective (−2k = n+a+2 ≥ n+d+1).

(ii) If L is not ⌈(−n−1−b)/2⌉-connective, put l = ⌈(−n−1−b)/2⌉ − 1, N′ := Ω^{n+1}Dτ_{≤l}L and f : N′ → N dual to L → τ_{≤l}L; the same estimate shows Ω^{n+1}Q(N′) is (−1)-truncated (max(n+1+2l+d, l+d−r) < 0), giving a Lagrangian surgery datum (HK.3/lagrangian-surgery); the new Lagrangian L′ = cofib(N′ → τ_{≥l+1}L) is (l+1)-connective.
Bijectivity of L^{a,b}_n → L_n follows as in HK.4/quadratic-surgery.

r = ∞, d = 0: symmetric surgery for a duality exchanging the two halves, which gives the Witt groups of the heart (GN §6.8a `symmetricHeartLTheory`).

nodes.statement: Let R be coherent of global dimension d, M invertible and Q an r-symmetric M-compatible Poincaré structure on D^p(R). For n ≥ d − 2r: if n + d is even, L^{d,d}_n(R;Q) → L_n(R;Q) is an isomorphism; if n + d is odd, L^{d−1,d}_n(R;Q) → L_n(R;Q) is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Odd vanishing and Witt groups in global dimension at most one
nodes.statement: Let R be coherent of global dimension d, M invertible and Q r-symmetric and M-compatible. (i) If d = 0, L_{2k−1}(R;Q) = 0 for every k ≥ 1 − r. (ii) If d ≤ 1, L_{2k}(R;Q) ≅ W(Proj(R); Ω^{2k}Q(Ω^k −)) for every k ≥ 1 − r, via (P,q) ↦ (P[−k],q). For Q = Q^{≥m}_M (r = 2 − m), π_{2k}Q^{≥m}_M(P[−k]) ≅ π₀Q^{≥m−k}_{(−1)^kM}(P), so the Witt group is that of (−1)^k-quadratic forms for k = m − 2, (−1)^k-even forms for k = m − 1 and (−1)^k-symmetric forms for k ≥ m; the L-group statement covers k ≥ m − 1 only, the case k = m − 2 being HK.4/witt-group-computes-L0 (iii) transported by HK.1/bordism-invariant-periodicity. If d = 0 (R semisimple) the odd symmetric and quadratic L-groups vanish in all degrees; for a field K of characteristic ≠ 2, L^q_{4k+2}(K) ≅ L^s_{4k+2}(K) = 0; and the heart of D^p(R) is Proj(R), whose symmetric Witt group is W(Proj(R);Q^gs_M).
hypotheses: R left-coherent; k ≥ 1 − r in (i) and (ii).
proofSteps: (i) HK.6/symmetric-surgery with d = 0, (a,b) = (−1,0), n = 2k−1: the condition a ≥ −n − 2r reads k ≥ 1 − r; Pn^{−1}_n is contractible (HK.3/bounded-l-monoids).

(ii) HK.6/coherent-symmetric-surgery with d = 1 (n = 2k, n + d odd) gives L_{2k} ≅ L^{0,1}_{2k}; HK.3/widen-lagrangian-bound gives L^{0,1}_{2k} ≅ L^{0,0}_{2k}; shifting by k and HK.3/strictly-metabolic-witt identify L^{0,0}_{2k} with W(Proj(R);Ω^{2k}Q(Ω^k−)). A ring of global dimension 0 also satisfies the hypotheses with d = 1, so the same argument applies.
The value on P[−k] follows from HK.0/shift-periodicity, and the classical form groups from GN §6.8a (m − k = 2, 1, ≤ 0).

Semisimple rings: Q^s_M is r-symmetric for all r, giving all odd symmetric groups; for the quadratic ones reduce by HK.1/bordism-invariant-periodicity to L^q_{−3}(R;M′), which is L^gs_{−3}(R;M′) by HK.4/quadratic-low-degree-comparison, and vanishes by (i) with k = −1 ≥ 1 − 2.
For a field of characteristic ≠ 2, L^s_{4k+2} is the Witt group of antisymmetric forms, which have symplectic bases and so Lagrangians.
acceptance: R = ℤ (d = 1), Q = Q^gs (r = 2), k = 0: L^gs_0(ℤ) is the Witt group of symmetric forms, ℤ by signature.
R = 𝔽₂, Q = Q^{≥1} (r = 1), k = 0: L^ge_0(𝔽₂) is the Witt group of even forms, which is 0.

nodes.title: Comparison of an r-symmetric flavour with symmetric L-theory
nodes.statement: Let R be coherent of global dimension d, M invertible and Q an r-symmetric M-compatible Poincaré structure on D^p(R). Then L_n(R;Q) → L_n(R;Q^s_M) = L^s_n(R;M) is injective for n ≥ d − 2r + 2 and bijective for n ≥ d − 2r + 3.
hypotheses: R left-coherent of global dimension d; Q r-symmetric.
proofSteps: Compare L^{d,d}_n (n + d even) or L^{d−1,d}_n (n + d odd) for Q and Q^s_M; by HK.6/coherent-symmetric-surgery both compute L_n (Q^s_M is r-symmetric for all r).

Bijectivity for n ≥ d − 2r + 3: the bounded groups agree by HK.4/genuine-symmetric-bounded-agreement, whose conditions a ≤ n + 2r − 4, b ≤ n + 2r − 3 hold for (a,b) = (d,d) (using the parity of n − d) and (d−1,d).

Injectivity at n = d − 2r + 2 (so n + d even, (a,b) = (d,d)): by exactness in the middle (HK.6/symmetric-surgery) it suffices that a (−d+r−1)-connective Q-Poincaré object whose symmetric image has a (−d+r−1)-connective Lagrangian L has a Q-Lagrangian. The fibre of Ω^nQ(L) → Ω^nQ^s_M(L) is (−1)-truncated by r-symmetry, so the map is injective on π₀ and onto on π₁, and the Lagrangian lifts.
acceptance: Q = Q^gs_M (r = 2): injective n ≥ d − 2, bijective n ≥ d − 1.
Q = Q^gq_M (r = 0): injective n ≥ d + 2, bijective n ≥ d + 3.

sources.match: Proves that for an r-symmetric structure over a coherent ring of global dimension d the map to symmetric L-theory is injective from degree d − 2r + 2 and bijective from d − 2r + 3, by comparing bounded L-groups and lifting Lagrangians.

nodes.title: Theorem 6: comparison of the genuine flavours
nodes.statement: Let R be coherent of global dimension d and M invertible. Then L^gs_n(R;M) → L^s_n(R;M) and GW^gs_n(R;M) → GW^s_n(R;M) are injective for n ≥ d − 2 and bijective for n ≥ d − 1; L^gq_n(R;M) → L^s_n(R;M) and GW^gq_n(R;M) → GW^s_n(R;M) are injective for n ≥ d + 2 and bijective for n ≥ d + 3; and L^gq_n(R;M) → L^gs_n(R;M) is injective for n ≥ d + 2 and bijective for n ≥ d + 3. For non-negative n this improves Ranicki's comparison for Noetherian rings of global dimension d (injective for n ≥ 2d − 3, bijective for n ≥ 2d − 2), through Theorem 5.
hypotheses: R left-coherent of global dimension d.
proofSteps: L-theory: HK.7/symmetric-comparison-range with r = 2 for Q^gs_M and r = 0 for Q^gq_M (HK.2/genuine-family-bounds).

GW: the identity functors (D^p(R),Q^gq_M) → (D^p(R),Q^gs_M) → (D^p(R),Q^s_M) are Poincaré functors with the same duality, so they induce equivalences on K(R;M)_{hC₂}; by the fundamental fibre sequence K_{hC₂} → GW → L (GN §6.8a `stableGWFundamentalSquare`) the squares from GW to L are cartesian and the cofibres of the GW maps are those of the L maps. The source attributes this to Theorem 1; the input is the fibre sequence of Paper II (sourceIssues E5).
L^gq_n → L^gs_n: compose with L^gs_n → L^s_n, which is bijective for n ≥ d − 1 ≤ d + 2.
Comparison with Ranicki: identify L^gs_n with L^short_n for n ≥ 0 (HK.4/ranicki-genuine-symmetric); d − 1 ≤ 2d − 2 for d ≥ 1.
acceptance: d = 0 (semisimple): L^gs_n ≅ L^s_n for n ≥ −1.
R = ℤ (d = 1): L^gs_n ≅ L^s_n for n ≥ 0 and L^gq_n ≅ L^gs_n for n ≥ 4, consistent with GN §6.10a's sharper ℤ-ranges.
