nodes.title: Sharpness and non-optimality of the comparison ranges
nodes.statement: The bijectivity bound n ≥ d − 1 for L^gs → L^s is sharp: for the d-dimensional ring 𝔽₂[ℤ^d] with the involution induced by inversion, L^gs → L^s is not surjective on π_{d−2}. Similarly, for ε = −1, L^gs_0(ℤ[ℤ];ε) → L^s_0(ℤ[ℤ];ε) is not surjective. For d = 0 the example shows sharpness also for commutative rings with trivial involution, and L^gs(ℤ/4) → L^s(ℤ/4) fails to be an isomorphism on almost all positive homotopy groups. On the other hand, for many regular Noetherian domains of arbitrary finite Krull dimension L^gs → L^s is an isomorphism on π_n for all n ≥ −1, so among regular rings the bounds are far from optimal.
hypotheses: The Ranicki–Shaneson splitting L(R[ℤ];Q) ≃ L(R;Q) ⊕ ΣL(R;Q) for Q = Q^gs, Q^s when K₀(R) ≅ K₀(R[ℤ]) ≅ ℤ is an imported input (Ranicki; Milgram–Ranicki; reproved in Paper IV), recorded as a gap.
proofSteps: By the Ranicki–Shaneson splitting and induction, Σ^dL^gs(𝔽₂) → Σ^dL^s(𝔽₂) is a retract of L^gs(𝔽₂[ℤ^d]) → L^s(𝔽₂[ℤ^d]).

So it suffices that L^gs_{−2}(𝔽₂) → L^s_{−2}(𝔽₂) is not surjective: L^s_{−2}(𝔽₂) ≅ L^s_2(𝔽₂) ≅ ℤ/2 by 2-periodicity, while L^gs_{−2}(𝔽₂) = 0 (HK.7/field-l-groups). The source writes 'L^gs(𝔽₂) = 0' for the latter (sourceIssues E4).
The ε = −1 statement over ℤ[ℤ] follows by the same retract argument from degree −1 over ℤ; the ℤ/4 and regular-ring statements are quoted (Read, Corollary F; Schlichting 2025).
acceptance: The example shows that the bijectivity bound d − 1 for L^gs → L^s cannot be improved; since the comparison maps are compatible with L^gq ≃ Σ⁴L^gs and L^s ≃ Σ⁴L^s (HK.1/bordism-invariant-periodicity), the bound d + 3 for L^gq → L^s cannot be improved either. The source presents this as sharpness of the bounds of Corollary 1.3.10; the injectivity bounds are not addressed by the example.

sources.match: Shows the comparison bounds are sharp using 𝔽₂[ℤ^d] and the Ranicki–Shaneson splitting, gives the ε = −1 example over ℤ[ℤ], cites Read for ℤ/4, and cites Schlichting for the non-optimality over regular Noetherian domains.

nodes.title: The right-handed versions
nodes.statement: If R is right-coherent of finite right global dimension d, the conclusions of HK.6/low-dimension-witt (including Ranicki's vanishing), HK.7/symmetric-comparison-range and HK.7/genuine-comparison-theorem hold for R.
hypotheses: R right-coherent of right global dimension d.
proofSteps: Apply the left-handed results to R^op with Q^∨ (HK.0/opposite-ring-transport), which is r-symmetric when Q is (HK.2/opposite-ring-bounds).
Transport along (D^p(R^op),Q^∨) ≃ (D^p(R),Q).

nodes.title: The Dedekind case
nodes.statement: Let R be a Dedekind ring (for instance a ring of integers of a number field) and M invertible. Then L^gs_n(R;M) → L^s_n(R;M) and GW^gs_n(R;M) → GW^s_n(R;M) are injective for n = −1 and bijective for n ≥ 0; in particular the non-negative homotopy groups of L^gs(R;M) are 4-periodic. Likewise L^gq_n → L^s_n and GW^gq_n → GW^s_n are injective for n = 3 and bijective for n ≥ 4. With the Hebestreit–Steimle comparison this gives GW^s_cl(R;M) ≃ τ_{≥0}GW^s(R;M) and τ_{≥4}GW^q_cl(R;M) ≃ τ_{≥4}GW^s(R;M) (GN §6.8a, Corollary 1.3.15).
hypotheses: R Dedekind (hereditary Noetherian domain, global dimension ≤ 1).
proofSteps: Dedekind rings are Noetherian of global dimension ≤ 1 (HK.6/coherent-global-dimension); apply HK.7/genuine-comparison-theorem with d = 1.
4-periodicity of L^s (HK.1/bordism-invariant-periodicity) transfers to L^gs in non-negative degrees.
The GW consequences are the statement GN §6.8a records as Corollary 1.3.15.
acceptance: L^gs_n(ℤ) for n ≥ 0 is ℤ, ℤ/2, 0, 0 periodically.
L^gs_{−1}(ℤ) → L^s_{−1}(ℤ) = 0 is injective, so L^gs_{−1}(ℤ) = 0.

sources.match: Specialises the comparison ranges to Dedekind rings, deduces 4-periodicity of non-negative genuine symmetric L-groups, and with Hebestreit–Steimle identifies classical symmetric GW with the connective cover of homotopy symmetric GW and quadratic GW above degree 4.

nodes.title: The improvement for 2-torsion-free rings
nodes.statement: Let R be commutative, coherent of global dimension d, with M = R. Then Σ²L^gs(R) ≃ L^{−ge}(R) and Σ²L^ge(R) ≃ L^{−gq}(R). If R is moreover 2-torsion free (for instance a Dedekind domain with fraction field of characteristic ≠ 2), Q^{−ge} → Q^{−gs} and Q^gq → Q^ge are equivalences, so Σ²L^gs(R) ≃ L^{−gs}(R) and Σ²L^gq(R) ≃ L^{−gq}(R), compatibly with the comparison map; hence L^gq_n(R) → L^gs_n(R) and GW^q_{cl,n}(R) → GW^s_{cl,n}(R) are injective for n = d and bijective for n ≥ d + 1.
hypotheses: R commutative, coherent of global dimension d, 2-torsion free; M = R with trivial involution.
proofSteps: The two double-shift equivalences are HK.1/bordism-invariant-periodicity with (M,m) = (R,0) and (R,1).
Q^{−ge} = Q^{−gs} and Q^gq = Q^ge by HK.0/tate-collapse-criterion (R[2] = 0).

So L^gq(R) → L^gs(R) is Ω² of L^{−gq}(R) → L^{−gs}(R); HK.7/genuine-comparison-theorem for M = R(−1) gives injectivity in degree d+2 and bijectivity from d+3 for the latter, i.e. degrees d and d+1 for the former.
Transfer to classical GW by the cartesian squares and the Hebestreit–Steimle comparison (GN §6.8a).
acceptance: For R = ℤ (d = 1): GW^q_{cl,n}(ℤ) → GW^s_{cl,n}(ℤ) is injective for n = 1 and bijective for n ≥ 2, matching GN §6.11's quadratic table (GW₁ = (ℤ/2)², symmetrisation iso from degree 2).

sources.match: Uses the double-shift equivalences and the collapse of genuine structures for 2-torsion-free rings to show the quadratic-to-symmetric comparison gains two degrees, proving the second part of Theorem 3.

nodes.title: Genuine Poincaré structures of form parameters
nodes.statement: A form parameter λ on (R,M) (Bak, Baues, Schlichting) is a quadratic R-module Q_λ with maps M_{C₂} →^τ Q_λ →^ρ M^{C₂} composing to the trace, whose R-action has cross-effect (a ⟂ b)x = τ((a⊗b)ρ(x)); a λ-hermitian form on P ∈ Proj(R) is a σ-symmetric M-valued form φ with a map q : P → Q_λ such that q(rv) = r·q(v), q(v+u) − q(v) − q(u) = τ(φ(v,u)) and ρ q(v) = φ(v,v). The functor P ↦ {λ-hermitian forms on P} extends as a non-abelian derived functor to a Poincaré structure Q^{gλ}_M on D^p(R) with duality Hom_R(−,M). Q_λ = M^{C₂}, M_{C₂} and im(M_{C₂} → M^{C₂}) give Q^gs, Q^gq and Q^ge. Since Q^{gλ}_M(P[0]) is discrete, Q^{gλ}_M is 0-quadratic and 0-symmetric (1- or 2-symmetric, resp. 1- or 2-quadratic, in the even and symmetric, resp. even and quadratic, cases). For R coherent of global dimension ≤ 1, L^{gλ}_n(R) → L^s_n(R) is injective for n = 3 and bijective for n ≥ 4, and L^{gλ}_2(R) is the Witt group of the form parameter (−M, ker(M → Q_λ)).
hypotheses: R with an invertible ℤ-module with involution M; R coherent of global dimension ≤ 1 for the comparison claims (the source writes '1-dimensional ring'; corrected, sourceIssues E7).
proofSteps: Schlichting's equivalence between form parameters and reduced degree-two polynomial functors on Proj(R) gives the functor of λ-hermitian forms; extend by Calmès et al. I, Proposition 4.2.18 (non-abelian derivation) to D^p(R).
Discreteness of values on P[0] gives fibre and cofibre to Q^s_M and from Q^q_M concentrated so that the structure is 0-symmetric and 0-quadratic (HK.2/r-symmetric-m-quadratic).
Comparison: HK.7/symmetric-comparison-range with r = 0 and d = 1.
Degree two: HK.6/low-dimension-witt (ii) with k = 1 ≥ 1 − r; Ω²Q^{gλ}(Ω−) on projectives is the form-parameter functor for (−M, ker(M → Q_λ)).
acceptance: Q_λ = M^{C₂} recovers the symmetric case, where the ranges improve to those of Q^gs.

sources.match: Associates a genuine Poincaré structure to every form parameter, notes it is 0-quadratic and 0-symmetric and in the classical cases more, and derives the comparison range for one-dimensional rings and the degree-two Witt description.

nodes.title: L-theory of the Burnside form parameter over ℤ
nodes.statement: Let Q^b on D^p(ℤ) be the pullback of Q^gs(X) → Hom_ℤ(X,τ_{≥0}ℤ^{tC₂}) along Hom_ℤ(X,τ_{≥1/2}ℤ^{tC₂}), where τ_{≥1/2}ℤ^{tC₂} := ℤ ×_{ℤ/2} τ_{≥0}ℤ^{tC₂}. It is the Poincaré structure of the Burnside form parameter (Q_λ = ℤ ×_{ℤ/2} ℤ, M = ℤ, M → Q_λ = (2,0)). Then L^b_n(ℤ) → L^s_n(ℤ) is an isomorphism for n ≥ 2; L^u_n(𝕊) → L^b_n(ℤ) is an isomorphism for n ≤ 0 and onto for n = 1; and L^q_1(ℤ) → L^b_1(ℤ) is onto, so L^b_1(ℤ) = 0. Hence L^b_n(ℤ) = L^s_n(ℤ) for n ≥ 2, L^b_1(ℤ) = 0 and L^b_n(ℤ) = L^u_n(𝕊) for n ≤ 0.
hypotheses: Over ℤ with trivial involution.
proofSteps: By HK.7/form-parameter-structures with d = 1, L^b_n(ℤ) → L^s_n(ℤ) is injective for n = 3 and bijective for n ≥ 4; as L^s_3(ℤ) = 0 it is bijective at n = 3. At n = 2, since M → Q_λ is injective, L^b_2(ℤ) is the Witt group of the form parameter (−ℤ, 0), i.e. of symplectic forms over ℤ, which vanishes, as does L^s_2(ℤ).
The Poincaré functor (Mod^ω_𝕊, Q^u) → (D^p(ℤ), Q^b) has 1-connective map on linear parts 𝕊 → τ_{≥1/2}ℤ^{tC₂}; HK.5/connective-comparison with p = 1, m = 0 gives iso for n ≤ 0 and onto for n = 1.

For L^b_1: represent a class on X in degrees [−1,0]; π₀X is free; surgery along π₀(X) → X leaves a Poincaré object of ΩQ^b with homology a torsion group T in degree −1, on which the form lifts to ΩQ^q because π₀Ωhom_ℤ(T[−1], τ_{≥1/2}ℤ^{tC₂}) = 0 for torsion T; as L^q_1(ℤ) = 0, L^b_1(ℤ) = 0.
acceptance: The structure sits between Q^gq_ℤ and Q^gs_ℤ; L^b was first studied by Dotto–Ogle.

sources.match: Defines the Burnside Poincaré structure on D^p(ℤ), compares its L-theory with symmetric L-theory in degrees ≥ 2 and with universal L-theory of the sphere in degrees ≤ 1, and shows L^b_1(ℤ) vanishes by surgery and lifting to the quadratic structure.

nodes.title: L-groups of a field in every flavour
nodes.statement: Let K be a field and M = K with an involution of sign ε. (a) For every r-symmetric Q and k ≥ 1 − r, L_{2k−1}(K;Q) = 0 and L_{2k}(K;Q) ≅ W(Proj(K); Ω^{2k}Q(Ω^k−)); in particular all odd L^s and L^q groups vanish. (b) If char K ≠ 2, all flavours coincide; for ε = +1, L^s_{4k}(K) = W(K) (the Witt ring of QuadraticFormInvariants Layer 4) and L^s_{4k+2}(K) = 0, and for ε = −1 the two residues are exchanged, L^s_{n+2}(K;−1) ≅ L^s_n(K;+1). (c) If char K = 2, −M = M and L^s, L^q, K^{tC₂} are 2-periodic; L^s_{2k}(K) is the Witt group W^s(K) of symmetric bilinear forms and L^q_{2k}(K) the Witt group W^q(K) of quadratic forms; L^gs_n(K) → L^s_n(K) is an isomorphism for n ≥ −1, L^gs_n(K) ≅ L^q_n(K) for n ≤ −3, and L^gs_{−2}(K) = L^ge_0(K) = 0 because even forms in characteristic 2 are alternating and hence metabolic. For K = 𝔽₂: L^s_{2k}(𝔽₂) = ℤ/2 (rank mod 2), L^q_{2k}(𝔽₂) = ℤ/2 (Arf invariant), L^gs_{−2}(𝔽₂) = 0.
hypotheses: K a field; involution trivial up to sign.
proofSteps: (a) HK.6/low-dimension-witt with d = 0.

(b) 2 is a unit, so HK.0/tate-collapse-criterion makes all flavours equal; for ε = +1, L^s_{4k+2} = 0 by HK.6/low-dimension-witt and L^s_0 = W(K) by HK.4/witt-group-computes-L0 and QuadraticFormInvariants Layer 4; the case ε = −1 follows from L(K;Q^s_M) ≃ Ω²L(K;Q^s_{−M}) (HK.1/bordism-invariant-periodicity).

(c) Periodicity by HK.1/bordism-invariant-periodicity with −M = M. The comparison L^gs → L^s for n ≥ −1 is HK.7/genuine-comparison-theorem with d = 0; L^gs ≅ L^q for n ≤ −3 is HK.4/quadratic-low-degree-comparison; L^gs_{−2}(K) ≅ L^ge_0(K;−M) = L^ge_0(K) by HK.1/bordism-invariant-periodicity, which is the Witt group of even forms (HK.4/witt-group-computes-L0 (ii)), and an even form b = c + c^t satisfies b(x,x) = 2c(x,x) = 0, so it is alternating, has a symplectic basis and is metabolic.
For 𝔽₂: W^s(𝔽₂) = ℤ/2 via rank mod 2, and W^q(𝔽₂) = ℤ/2 via the Arf invariant.
acceptance: L^s_{−2}(𝔽₂) = ℤ/2 ≠ 0 = L^gs_{−2}(𝔽₂): this is the input to the sharpness example HK.7/sharpness-examples.
For K = ℝ, L^s_0(ℝ) = ℤ by signature.

Uses L^s_2(𝔽₂) ≅ ℤ/2 and the vanishing of genuine symmetric L-theory of 𝔽₂ in degree −2 (corrected; sourceIssues E4).

nodes.title: Theorem 1: the fibre sequence for classical symmetric Grothendieck–Witt theory
nodes.statement: For every associative ring R and every duality D = Hom_R(−,M) on Proj(R) given by an invertible ℤ-module with involution M, there is a natural fibre sequence of connective spectra K(R;M)_{hC₂} →^{hyp} GW^s_cl(R;M) → L^short(R;M), where GW^s_cl(R;M) is the group completion of the groupoid of unimodular M-valued symmetric forms, K(R;M) carries the C₂-action P ↦ DP, and L^short(R;M) := τ_{≥0}L^gs(R;M) has π_nL^short(R;M) ≅ L^short_n(R;M), Ranicki's symmetric L-groups of n-dimensional Poincaré complexes. If 2 ∈ R^×, Ranicki's groups are 4-periodic and equal to the Witt groups, and the sequence is Schlichting's.
hypotheses: No hypothesis on R or on 2.
proofSteps: The fundamental fibre sequence K(D^p(R),Q)_{hC₂} → GW(D^p(R),Q) → L(D^p(R),Q) for Q = Q^gs_M (GN §6.8a `stableGWFundamentalSquare`).
K(R;M) is connective, so K(R;M)_{hC₂} is connective (RefinedTraceMethods RT.2/homotopy-orbits-fixed-points); hence π₀GW^gs → π₀L^gs is onto and τ_{≥0} preserves the fibre sequence.
τ_{≥0}GW^gs(R;M) ≃ GW^s_cl(R;M) by Hebestreit–Steimle (GN §6.8a `weightHeartGWComparison`), compatibly with hyp.
π_nτ_{≥0}L^gs(R;M) ≅ L^short_n(R;M) for n ≥ 0 by Theorem 5 (HK.4/ranicki-genuine-symmetric).
If 2 is a unit all genuine structures agree (HK.0/tate-collapse-criterion), L^s is 4-periodic (HK.1/bordism-invariant-periodicity) and its groups are Witt groups of forms and formations.
acceptance: R = ℤ on π₀: K₀(ℤ)_{C₂} = ℤ maps to GW^s_{cl,0}(ℤ) = ℤ⟨1⟩ ⊕ ℤ⟨−1⟩ by 1 ↦ ⟨1⟩ + ⟨−1⟩ (the hyperbolic plane), and the cokernel maps isomorphically to L^short_0(ℤ) = ℤ by the signature (a,b) ↦ a − b.
R a field of characteristic ≠ 2: on π₀, GW₀(K) → W(K) is onto with kernel the hyperbolic multiples, the classical Witt sequence.

sources.locator: Theorem 1, p. 2, and its derivation, pp. 3–4
sources.match: States the fibre sequence K(R;M)_{hC₂} → GW^s_cl(R;M) → L^short(R;M) for every ring and derives it from the fibre sequence of Paper II, Hebestreit–Steimle and Theorem 5; notes it is Schlichting's when 2 is a unit.
The fundamental fibre square of GW, L, K^{hC₂} and K^{tC₂}, hence the fibre sequence K_{hC₂} → GW → L.

nodes.title: The quadratic fibre sequence
nodes.statement: For every ring R and invertible M there is a fibre sequence K(R;M)_{hC₂} →^{hyp} GW^q_cl(R;M) → τ_{≥0}(Σ⁴L^gs(R;M)), where GW^q_cl is the group completion of unimodular M-valued quadratic forms.
hypotheses: No hypothesis on R or on 2.
proofSteps: Apply the fundamental fibre sequence (GN §6.8a) to Q^gq_M and take connective covers as in HK.8/classical-gw-fibre-sequence.
τ_{≥0}GW^gq(R;M) ≃ GW^q_cl(R;M) by Hebestreit–Steimle (GN §6.8a).
L^gq(R;M) ≃ Σ⁴L^gs(R;M) by applying HK.1/bordism-invariant-periodicity twice (Σ²L^gs_M ≃ L^ge_{−M} and Σ²L^ge_{−M} ≃ L^gq_M).
acceptance: R = ℤ: π₀ of the cofibre term is L^gs_{−4}(ℤ) = L^q_{−4}(ℤ) = ℤ (signature/8), and GW^q_{cl,0}(ℤ) = ℤ⊕ℤ is generated by the hyperbolic plane and E₈.

sources.match: Derives the quadratic fibre sequence with third term τ_{≥0}Σ⁴L^gs from the general fibre sequence, Hebestreit–Steimle and Σ⁴L^gs ≃ L^gq.

nodes.title: Karoubi's splitting after inverting 2
nodes.statement: After inverting 2, polarisation gives GW^q_cl(R;M)[1/2] ≃ GW^s_cl(R;M)[1/2], and there is a natural splitting GW^s_{cl,*}(R;M)[1/2] ≅ (K_*(R;M)[1/2])^{C₂} ⊕ W_*(R;M)[1/2], with K_* the K-groups with the duality action and W_* the 4-periodic Witt groups of symmetric forms (even degrees) and formations (odd degrees), here π_*L^s(R;M) in non-negative degrees.
hypotheses: Uses the two-inverted comparison L(R;Q^{≥m}_M)[1/2] ≃ L^s(R;M)[1/2] of GN §6.10b (CDH III Proposition 3.1.14), whose spectrum-level multiplicative input is GN's recorded gap (Paper IV).
proofSteps: Invert 2 in HK.8/classical-gw-fibre-sequence: π_*(K_{hC₂})[1/2] = (K_*[1/2])_{C₂} ≅ (K_*[1/2])^{C₂}.
The fundamental square splits after inverting 2: GW[1/2] ≃ K[1/2]_{hC₂} ⊕ L[1/2] (Calmès et al. II, Corollary 4.4.14).
L^gs[1/2] ≃ L^gq[1/2] ≃ L^s[1/2] (GN 6.10.6), so the quadratic and symmetric sequences agree after inverting 2 and the L-term has the 4-periodic Witt groups.
acceptance: R a field of characteristic ≠ 2: GW₀(K)[1/2] ≅ ℤ[1/2] ⊕ W(K)[1/2] via rank/2 and Witt class.

sources.match: Recalls Karoubi's splitting of symmetric GW after inverting 2 into the invariants of K-theory and the Witt groups, and states that the fibre sequence of Theorem 1 recovers it.
Gives the natural splitting GW(C,Q)[1/2] ≃ K(C,Q)[1/2]^{hC₂} ⊕ L(C,Q)[1/2].

nodes.title: Theorem 3: quadratic versus symmetric Grothendieck–Witt groups
nodes.statement: Let R be coherent of global dimension d and M invertible. Then the polarisation map GW^q_{cl,n}(R;M) → GW^s_{cl,n}(R;M) is injective for n ≥ d + 2 and an isomorphism for n ≥ d + 3. If moreover R is commutative and 2-torsion free and M = R, it is injective for n ≥ d and an isomorphism for n ≥ d + 1. The same holds for right-coherent rings of finite right global dimension, and the first statement (ranges d + 2 and d + 3) holds with the Grothendieck–Witt groups of any form parameter in place of quadratic forms.
hypotheses: R left-coherent of global dimension d (or right-coherent of right global dimension d).
proofSteps: For n ≥ 0, GW^q_{cl,n} = GW^gq_n and GW^s_{cl,n} = GW^gs_n (Hebestreit–Steimle, GN §6.8a).
By HK.7/genuine-comparison-theorem, GW^gq_n → GW^s_n is injective for n ≥ d+2 and bijective for n ≥ d+3, and GW^gs_n → GW^s_n is bijective for n ≥ d − 1; compose.
The 2-torsion-free improvement is HK.7/two-torsion-free-improvement.
Right-coherent rings: HK.7/right-coherent-version; form parameters: HK.7/form-parameter-structures with the same cartesian-square argument.
acceptance: R = ℤ (d = 1, 2-torsion free): bijective for n ≥ 2 and injective at n = 1, matching GN §6.11 (GW^q_1(ℤ) = (ℤ/2)², GW^s_1(ℤ) = (ℤ/2)³).
The source makes no sharpness claim for Theorem 3 itself; HK.7/sharpness-examples concerns the L-theoretic comparisons L^gs → L^s and L^gq → L^s.

sources.locator: Theorem 3, p. 3; Corollary 1.3.10, pp. 30–31; Remarks 1.3.12, 1.3.16 and 1.3.17, pp. 31–32
sources.match: States the quadratic-to-symmetric comparison for coherent rings of finite global dimension with its 2-torsion-free improvement, and proves it from the L-theoretic comparison, the cartesian squares and the two-degree shift, with right-coherent and form-parameter versions.

sourceIssues.printed: Parts (i) and (ii) refer to Poincaré objects of D^p(R) with Q[−n], although the hypotheses concern a general stable ∞-category C with a t-structure.
sourceIssues.correction: Read C in place of D^p(R) in both parts, as the proof does.
sourceIssues.reason: The hypotheses introduce no ring; the proof works in C; Corollary 1.3.8 and the dévissage Theorem 2.2.4 apply the proposition to categories that are not D^p of a discrete ring.
1.1.6 is a lemma and is cited as such elsewhere in the paper.

sourceIssues.printed: The argument concludes from L^s_2(𝔽₂) ≅ ℤ/2 and the vanishing of the genuine symmetric L-theory of 𝔽₂ written without a degree.
sourceIssues.correction: The needed and true statement is L^gs_{−2}(𝔽₂) = 0, against L^s_{−2}(𝔽₂) ≅ L^s_2(𝔽₂) ≅ ℤ/2.
sourceIssues.reason: L^gs_0(𝔽₂) is the symmetric Witt group of 𝔽₂, which is ℤ/2, so the whole spectrum does not vanish; in degree −2, L^gs_{−2}(𝔽₂) ≅ L^ge_0(𝔽₂) is the Witt group of even forms, which vanishes since even forms in characteristic 2 are alternating and hence metabolic (HK.7/field-l-groups).

sourceIssues.correction: The squares are cartesian by the fundamental fibre sequence (1) of Paper II (Corollary [II].4.4.13) applied to the identity Poincaré functors between these structures, which share the duality and hence the term K(R;M)_{hC₂}.

sourceIssues.printed: The remark identifies the relevant Tate cohomology group with homomorphisms from P to the 2-torsion of R, a skew-symmetric b going to x ↦ b(x,x).
sourceIssues.correction: The 2-torsion R[2] must carry the Frobenius-twisted module structure r·a = r²a (the structure on π₀ of HR(−1)^{tC₂} from the Tate diagonal).
sourceIssues.reason: b(rx,rx) = r²b(x,x), so x ↦ b(x,x) is not R-linear for the usual structure (e.g. R = 𝔽₂[t], b(x,y) = xy gives x ↦ x²). The conclusion that symplectic forms are the (−1)-even ones is unaffected.

sourceIssues.printed: The comparison range and the degree-two Witt description are stated for a form parameter over a 1-dimensional ring.
